However, a direct and improper combination of these two tools can introduce significant bias, especially under high time resolution. This phenomenon is referred to as the “failure probability curse.” This paper analyzes the fundamental cause of this issue and proposes a conditional-probability correction method for the sequential Monte Carlo simulation. The method can eliminate the inherent bias from high-time-resolution sampling in power outage risk analysis and reconcile sequential Monte Carlo with different physical failure mechanisms. Furthermore, the conditional-probability perspective provided in this paper offers support and explanation for related existing methods at the level of mathematical principles, enhancing the insights of the “failure probability curse” from both an explanation and solution perspective. Numerical experiments based on an illustrative system and the Tennessee power network confirm the validity of the proposed approach.

title: Model Predictive Torque Control Using Modified TSF and Parameter Adjustment of SRMs for Torque Ripple Reduction
abstract: This article introduces a model predictive torque control (MPTC) scheme using a modified hybrid torque sharing function (TSF) and the adaptive adjustment regarding parameters for switched reluctance motors (SRMs) to mitigate the torque ripple effect and enhance dynamic performance. Compared with classic TSF control, torque model prediction is adopted in MPTC instead of hysteresis control to reduce torque ripple. First, an enhanced hybrid TSF is designed for torque ripple suppression, where the rising reference phase torque can be adjusted in real-time according to the actual phase torque in the demagnetizing interval. Second, adaptive adjustment of angles based on the approximate model and the look-up table is utilized to further minimize torque ripple under multiple operating conditions. Then, the linear active disturbance rejection control with the adaptive bandwidth parameter is applied to the speed controller for better dynamic performance under multiple operating conditions. Eventually, experiments on a 12/8 SRM are conducted to ascertain the efficacy of the proposed MTPC by comparison.

title: Sensorless Control of Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Improved Synchronous Reference Frame Filter in Double Angle Axis
abstract: In the medium-to-high-speed speed control system of the interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM), to address the issues of large harmonic component of the expanded back electromotive force (EMF) observed by conventional sliding mode observer (SMO) and the phase lag caused by the low-pass filter (LPF), a sensorless control method based on an improved synchronous reference frame filter (ISRFF) in double angle axis is proposed. Firstly, the extended back EMF in double angle and αβ-axis are processed through the LPF with same cut-off frequency to generate leading and lagging phase shifts. Secondly, the phase shifts are transformed to dq-axis, and the harmonics are filtered out by LPF. Then, the phase shifts are eliminated by a triangular transformation. The position observation accuracy of the SMO is improved while the rotor position error signal is constructed, thus the heterodyne method is omitted. Finally, the experimental results confirm that compared with conventional methods, the proposed method effectively filters out harmonics, reduces the maximum position error under steady-state conditions, and mitigates speed fluctuations during dynamic operation.

title: An Efficient Algorithm to Calculate Locational Marginal Emissions in ACOPF via Adjoint Optimization Reformulation
abstract: This letter proposes a locally exact adjoint method to compute the locational marginal emissions (LMEs) in AC optimal power flow (ACOPF). Unlike conventional sensitivity analysis based on repeated load perturbations, the proposed method derives LMEs by linearizing the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions at the cost-minimizing equilibrium. We show that all-bus LMEs can be recovered simultaneously by solving a single reduced sparse linear system. Numerical results on the IEEE 118-bus and 2383-bus systems with heterogeneous thermal and renewable generation demonstrate that the proposed method captures clear spatial and temporal variation of LMEs effectively.

title: Fully Distributed Fault-Tolerant Secondary Control for Islanded Microgrids With Actuator Faults and Disturbances
abstract: This paper investigates the secondary control problem of AC islanded microgrids (MG) with unknown external disturbances and actuator faults. A fully distributed fault-tolerant secondary control strategy based on adaptive dynamic event-triggered mechanism (DETM) is proposed to address voltage and frequency deviations caused by droop control, achieving active power sharing while effectively reducing the communication burden. Considering the possibility of actuator faults, adaptive laws are introduced to estimate and compensate for fault parameters, thereby improving the system’s fault tolerance. The designed adaptive law and event-triggered mechanism (ETM) are implemented based on a fully distributed framework and do not rely on any global information. Compared with existing work, this paper introduces time-varying auxiliary functions and trigger functions, and obtains a strictly positive minimum trigger interval (MTI) without using global information, thus completely avoiding Zeno behavior in the presence of disturbances, which is more rigorous than simply theoretically excluding Zeno behavior. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is illustrated by simulation examples.

title: Dynamic Reserve Sizing With Statistically Feasible Guarantees: An Uncertainty-Adaptive Robust Optimization Framework
abstract: The integration of intermittent renewable energy and increasing load volatility necessitates adaptive reserve sizing frameworks to balance grid reliability and economic efficiency. Static reserve allocation methods struggle with dynamic uncertainty, risking high costs or compromised security. This study introduces a probabilistic reserve sizing framework with three innovations: 1) a dynamic architecture for economic dispatch and Unit Commitment (UC) employing a unified joint chance constraint to manage system-wide, temporally-coupled risks under uncertainty; 2) a dual-stage statistically feasible robust optimization (RO) approach employing a novel unified dimension-collapsing map, enabling tractable learning-calibrated uncertainty set construction with dimension-free out-of-sample reliability guarantees; and 3) a Learning-to-Optimize acceleration strategy that transforms the robust UC into a tractable linear program, enabling scalability. Validation on standard test systems up to 118 buses demonstrates the framework’s ability to dynamically adjust reserves through uncertainty-adaptive quantification. The solution reconciles statistical feasibility with computational efficiency, achieving scalable, cost-effective, and reliable operations. By integrating statistically feasible RO with machine learning acceleration, this framework provides a practical approach to managing uncertainty and ensuring economic and operational balance in power systems with high renewable penetration.

title: Stability Region Boundary of Multi-Parallel Grid-Following Converter Systems Considering Nonlinear Coupling Interactions
abstract: In multi-parallel grid-following voltage source converters (MGFL-VSCs), the nonlinear dynamics of the control loops and their coupling interactions substantially affect the transient synchronization stability (TSS) of MGFL-VSCs. This study focuses on the effects of nonlinear coupling interactions on TSS of the MGFL-VSC systems. First, on the basis of differential–algebraic equation–stability region boundary (SRB) theory, the study analyzes the effects of nonlinear dynamics and coupling interactions and plots the SRB of MGFL-VSCs. Results show that the coupling interactions limit the maximum phase angle of the phase-locked loop. The SRB of MGFL-VSCs consists of a stable manifold of unstable equilibrium points, a stable manifold of semi-singular points, and certain singular surfaces. The composition of SRB is closely related to the coupling interactions of nonlinear control. Second, on the basis of the correlation between SRB and transient instability modes, the transient instability modes of MGFL-VSCs are divided into traditional and coupling interaction instability modes, and the evolution of instability modes is systematically studied in consideration of nonlinear coupling interactions. In addition, an online assessment method that is based on the Port–Hamiltonian energy function is proposed. This method can quantitatively estimate the effect of coupling interactions on TSS by using the nonlinear normalized energy index. Finally, experimental and simulation results are provided to compare the proposed approach with existing methods and verify its effectiveness.

title: An MPC-Based Frequency Control Method Considering Nodal Frequency and RoCoF
abstract: The Centre of Inertia (COI) frequency and Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) are traditional indicators used in frequency measurement and control. With the increasing integration of inverter-based resources (IBRs), frequency exhibits more significant spatial characteristics, making COI frequency insufficient to represent frequency dynamics at specific locations. Meanwhile, protection devices such as Under-Frequency Load Shedding (UFLS), anti-islanding protection, and Fault-Ride-Through (FRT) rely on the nodal frequency or RoCoF. Consequently, there is a risk of protection device activations caused by discrepancies between system-level COI frequency or RoCoF and local protection triggering thresholds. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Model Predictive Control (MPC)-based approach that incorporates nodal frequency and RoCoF constraints. First, the nodal inertia calculation methodology, which was originally designed for systems with synchronous generators and grid-forming resources, is extended to include grid-following resources. Second, an MPC-based frequency control method was developed to restore nodal frequency, reduce RoCoF, and minimise the likelihood of unintended protection triggers. Lastly, the proposed strategy was validated through MATLAB–PSCAD co-simulations on IEEE test systems.

title: Wide-Area Power System Oscillations From Large-Scale AI Workloads
abstract: This paper develops a new dynamic power profiling approach for modeling AI-centric datacenter loads and analyzing their impact on grid operations, particularly their potential to induce wide-area grid oscillations. We characterize the periodic stochastic power fluctuations inherent to large-scale AI workloads during both the training and fine-tuning stages, driven by the state-of-the-art graphics processing unit (GPU) computing architecture design. These sustained, large power fluctuations, unlike conventional load ramping, act as persistent forcing inputs capable of interacting with and amplifying local and inter-area oscillation modes. Using the WECC 179-bus system and the NPCC 140-bus system, we have numerically studied the amplitude and variability of oscillatory responses under different factors. These factors include system strength, penetration level, fluctuation frequency range, individual datacenter size, geographical deployment, fluctuation suppression level, and workload ratio. Simulation results show that, notably, narrower fluctuation bands, larger single-site capacities, or dispersed siting can intensify oscillations across multiple modes. Our models and numerical studies provide a quantitative basis for integrating AI-dominant electricity demand into grid oscillation studies and further support the development of new planning and operational measures to power the growth of AI/computing load demands.

title: Dominant Transient Stability of the Co-Located PLL-Based Grid-Following Renewable Plant and Synchronous Condenser Systems
abstract: Deploying synchronous condensers (SynCons) near grid-following renewable energy sources (GFLRs) is an effective and increasingly adopted strategy for grid support. However, the potential transient instability risks in such configurations remain an open research question. This study investigates the mechanism of dominant synchronization instability source transition upon SynCon integration and proposes a straightforward approach to enhance system stability by leveraging their interactive characteristics. Firstly, a dual-timescale decoupling model is established, partitioning the system into a fast subsystem representing phase-locked loop (PLL) dynamics and a slow subsystem characterizing SynCon rotor dynamics. The study then examines the influence of SynCons on the transient stability of nearby PLLs and their own inherent stability. The study shows that SynCon's voltage-source characteristics and its time-scale separation from PLL dynamics can significantly enhance the PLL's stability boundary and mitigate non-coherent coupling effects among multiple GFLRs. However, the dominant instability source shifts from the fast-time-scale PLL to the slow-time-scale SynCon after SynCon integration. Crucially, this paper demonstrates that the damping effect of PLL control can also be transferred from the fast to the slow time scale, allowing well-tuned PLL damping to suppress SynCon rotor acceleration. Consequently, by utilizing SynCon's inherent support capability and a simple PLL damping loop, the transient stability of the co-located system can be significantly enhanced. These conclusions are validated using a converter controller-based Hardware-in-the-Loop (CHIL) platform.

title: A Data-Driven Approach for Coherency Identification in Large-Scale Power Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a temporal clustering–based approach for coherency identification in power grids that explicitly accounts for instrument transformer uncertainties and PMU measurement errors arising from communication failures. The method models the system using multiple single-bus–infinite-bus representations and introduces a metric for the electrical distance between physical system buses and a fictitious infinite bus, which is used to cluster buses into coherent groups. A key challenge of clustering-based methods—namely, the defining the clustering threshold—is systematically addressed by deriving a mathematically rigorous, power system–governed equation, resulting in a consistent method suitable for online applications. The effectiveness of the proposed data-driven approach is demonstrated using both simulated and real PMU signals, including scenarios with packet losses.

title: Time-Variant Nonlinear Participation Factors for Power Systems
abstract: The participation factor (PF) is a key metric for assessing the involvement of system states into an oscillation mode in power systems. A traditional linear PF has been effective in small-signal stability analysis and control, but it cannot capture the evolving and complex dynamics of a modern power system with significant nonlinearity. Existing nonlinear PFs account for inter-modal resonances up to a desired order but are assumed to be constant, not varying with the system’s response. This paper proposes a novel Time-Variant Nonlinear Participation Factor (TNPF), which unifies linear and nonlinear PFs within a single framework and enables reliable real-time quantification of the participation of state variables in a mode under disturbances, especially when nonlinear dynamics are non-negligible and the amplitude of state perturbations varies over time. To demonstrate the advantages of the TNPF, an adaptive control strategy is developed to dynamically activate a subset of distributed, highly participating battery-based damping controllers for efficient stabilization in response to disturbances. Case studies on the IEEE 39-bus system, including scenarios with high penetration of inverter-based resources, are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed TNPF.

title: Multi-Fidelity Dynamic Line Rating Fusion for System Load Margin Enhancement With Large-Scale Offshore Wind Generations
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-fidelity dynamic line rating (DLR) fusion method for power system load margin enhancement with large-scale offshore wind integration. First, multi-fidelity DLR data from diverse sensors are fused using multi-fidelity deep sigma point processes (MFDSPP), a probabilistic nonlinear learning model that integrates heterogeneous data sources to estimate the minimum line rating and quantify its uncertainty. Conformal prediction (CP), a distribution-free uncertainty calibration technique that refines prediction intervals using empirical residuals, is developed to refine the uncertainty intervals of DLRs. Then, continuation power flow (CPF) analysis is used to calculate the system's maximum load margin for numerous $N-k$ contingencies. Sampling these scenarios generates a large dataset to train the deep sigma point processes (DSPP) model, establishing a direct nonlinear relationship between operational data and load margin. Finally, DLR-based line capacity constraints and DSPP-derived load-margin constraints are integrated into the real-time control framework to improve system stability. Case studies on the Northeast Power Coordinating Council (NPCC) system, incorporating real DLR sensor measurements, authentic $N-k$ contingency datasets, and four real large-scale offshore wind farms, demonstrate that the proposed method effectively maintains a load margin greater than 10% of the base load, unlocks an additional 2,189.7 MWh of clean energy, reduces operating costs by approximately 2.34%, and achieves more than a 2,000 × speedup compared with classical CPF-based sensitivity methods.

title: Analysis of Power Swing Characteristics of Grid-Forming VSC System Considering the Current Limitation Mode
abstract: This paper investigates power swing characteristics of grid-forming (GFM) voltage source converter (VSC) systems with the current limitation mode in both non-inertial and inertial GFM-VSC systems. Following grid faults, non-inertial GFM-VSC systems can re-synchronize with the grid. However, they may experience significant power swings driven by their control dynamics. In contrast, inertial GFM-VSC systems may exhibit loss of synchronization (LOS), characterized by the divergence of the control-dependent angle from the active power control loop. These behaviors differ from those of conventional synchronous generator (SG)-based systems, in which power swings are typically characterized by physical angle deviations among power sources. Based on these findings, this paper examines the performance of traditional impedance-based swing-detection schemes in GFM-VSC systems. The theoretical analysis is validated through simulations covering both single- and multi-machine systems.

title: Stochastic Stability Oriented Frequency Control: A Probabilistic Forecasting-Based High-Order Stochastic Koopman Approach
abstract: The growing integration of intermittent renewables aggravates power imbalances between supply and demand, increasing the uncertainty of system frequency variations. Traditional deterministic frequency control schemes often overlook the impact of stochastic frequency fluctuations on system stability. This paper proposes an innovative stochastic stability-oriented model predictive control approach for system frequency regulation in the face of uncertainty of renewable generation. Firstly, a generic nonlinear stochastic dynamic model is established to precisely quantify time-evolutionary impacts of non-Gaussian uncertainty on system frequency dynamics. Subsequently, a high-order stochastic Koopman operator (HSKO) approach is developed by integrating high-order probabilistic forecasts with the Koopman theorem, serving as a powerful tool for global linearization of nonlinear stochastic dynamic models. Therefore, an interpretable optimal control law can be seamlessly derived in line with existing conclusions on stochastic stability identification, which originally breaks through the technical bottleneck of frequency stabilization for power systems with nonlinear stochastic dynamics. Comparative experiments with several state-of-the-art dynamic models and frequency control approaches demonstrate the superiority of the proposed HSKO approach in terms of model fidelity, control optimality, and frequency stability.

title: Cost-Oriented Scenario Reduction for Stochastic Optimization of Power System Operation With High-Penetration Renewable Energy
abstract: The growing uncertainty associated with renewable energy generation necessitates effective solutions addressing stochastic optimization of power system operations. Traditional stochastic optimization methods typically take scenario reduction as a preliminary step to alleviate computational burdens, which overlooks the connections between scenario reduction and stochastic optimization. This paper proposes a novel cost-oriented scenario reduction approach for stochastic optimal power flow (SOPF) to enhance the cost-effectiveness of operational decisions while maintaining system reliability. Firstly, an integrated scenario reduction and stochastic optimization (ISRSO) framework is established for SOPF, in which the reduced scenarios serve as a bridge between uncertainty quantification and uncertainty-aware optimization. Subsequently, a coordinated optimization model of scenario reduction and stochastic optimal power flow is formulated to jointly optimize the reduced scenarios and generation schedules, which preserves the probabilistic characteristics of the original scenarios and minimizes the operational cost of SOPF. Then, an alternating optimization algorithm is developed to convert the original nonconvex model into iterative convex problems with enhanced tractability. Simulation results on IEEE 14-bus and 118-bus test systems with realistic renewable energy generation data illustrate the statistical accuracy and cost-effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Engineering battery architectures for multifunctionality and high performance
abstract: Next-generation batteries demand architectural innovations that overcome the design limits of electrochemistry alone in conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). This review summarizes architectural design strategies for LIBs and emerging battery systems, classifying them into 1D fiber-based, 2D planar, and 3D architectures. 1D designs, such as coaxial fibers, twisted assemblies, and winding configurations, offer flexibility and mechanical resilience for wearable and microscale batteries. 2D architectures, including interdigitated, pillar-based, and mesh frameworks, are reviewed alongside deformable (serpentine and origami/kirigami) and nature-inspired (e.g., accordion-like) geometries that enhance stretchability and flexibility while preserving electrochemical performance. 3D structural batteries, focused on volumetric design and energy densification, are examined for their potential to combine mechanical resilience with electrochemical functionality. Each architectural class is assessed for its design principles, performance trade-offs, and fabrication feasibility. By correlating architectural designs with advancements in additive manufacturing, this review outlines pathways to address electro-chemo-mechanical coupling challenges and guide the development of next-generation architected batteries.

title: Overcoming the interfacial heterogeneity of pyramidal structure for efficient perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells
abstract: Submicron-textured silicon substrates introduce interfacial heterogeneity that compromises the performance of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells. To address this issue, we present an asymmetric phosphonic acid-based SAM (L30) bearing a thiophene group. This monolayer provides a conformal coating on the submicron-textured peaks and valleys, thereby uniformly covering the textured surfaces and establishing a stable buried interface. This molecular strategy effectively suppresses non-radiative recombination and contact losses, achieving a certified stabilized efficiency of 34.15% in the champion tandem device.

title: Thermal effects in perovskite solar cells
abstract: Heat accumulation remains a major threat to efficiency and operational stability as metal-halide perovskite photovoltaics are nearing commercial deployment. This perspective analyzes heat generation, consequences, and mitigation in representative 3D perovskite photovoltaics through a “source-implication-intervention” framework. We first examine waste heat from bias- and architecture-dependent optical and electrical losses, emphasizing reverse-bias hot spots and the intrinsically low thermal conductivity of soft, anharmonic lattices. We then discuss temperature-induced performance losses arising from recombination and diode characteristics, together with coupled degradation involving ion migration, interfacial reactions, electrode diffusion, and additive redistribution in charge-transport layers. Finally, thermal-management strategies are assessed, including thermally conductive additives, heat-radiation structures, interface engineering, functional encapsulation with conductive fillers or phase-change materials, and radiative-cooling covers that enhance mid-infrared emission with minimal optical loss. System-aware opportunities are further identified for tandem, flexible, and building-integrated perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Winding and Magnet Temperature Decoupled Tracking for PMSM Eliminating Saturation Using Small Position Signal Injection and Kalman Filter
abstract: This paper proposes a Kalman filter-based stator winding (SW) and permanent magnet (PM) temperature tracking approach for PM synchronous motors (PMSMs), where temperature tracking of SW and PM is decoupled and free from magnetic saturation and thus achieves improved performance. In the proposed approach, a small position signal is added to extract two decoupled temperature-sensitive measurements, a linear state-space model is constructed from the thermal model, and the Kalman filter is employed to accurately track the SW and PM temperatures by using the state-space model and measurements. The small position signal will not affect machine operation, while the temperature tracking can effectively avoid the cross influence between SW and PM. Moreover, there is no need for machine inductances and thus the temperature tracking is not affected by saturation as well as inverter distortion. In the proposed approach, the temperature tracking model includes secant and cosine operations of the current angle, which can effectively improve the signal-to-noise ratio especially under low-load conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated on a laboratory test machine with extensive experiments under various load and speed conditions.

title: Performance-Enhanced Adaptive Finite-Time Accurate Control of Uncertain Hydro Turbine Governing System With External Disturbances
abstract: The hydro turbine governing system (HTGS) plays a critical role in ensuring the overall stability and safe operation of hydropower stations. However, in the hydro turbine governing system, the rotor speed of the generator is the key factor affecting its performance. This paper proposes a finite time sliding mode control scheme aimed at achieving the accurate trajectory tracking of rotor speed to enhance the performance of the HTGS. To overcome the influence of external disturbances, a novel finite-time disturbance observer (FDO) is proposed. Unlike conventional high-order sliding-mode observers, the proposed FDO features a fully decoupled architecture that allows offline observer design and gain tuning independently of the controller synthesis. It requires only first-order differentiability of the lumped disturbances, and its estimation errors converge to zero strictly in finite time. This decoupled design enables exact trajectory tracking with stronger disturbance rejection, faster transient response, and lower online computational cost. Finally, a suite of extensive simulation outcomes is provided, which demonstrates the efficacy of the newly proposed control strategy. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves exact disturbance estimation within 1.2–1.5 s and drives the rotor speed tracking error to zero in 1.8–2.3 s, substantiating the finite-time convergence claim with quantitative metrics.

title: A Novel Digital Twin for Diesel Generator in Microgrids
abstract: Diesel generators (DiGs) play a vital role in Microgrids (MG) to ensure resiliency and reliability; however, accurate modeling of their behavior in both grid-connected and islanded modes is challenging due to limited experimental and manufacturer data. Standard simulation models often fail to capture real-world dynamics, leading to inaccurate results. To address these limitations, this paper presents an adaptive digital twin (DT) model for the 62.5 kVA DiG unit at the Center for Microgrid Research (CMR). The DT model, capable of grid-connected and islanded operations, is developed and experimentally validated within the CMR’s Microgrid infrastructure. The proposed DT leverages a novel adaptive parameter methodology to dynamically reflect the generator’s behavior in varying operating conditions for both transient and steady-state responses. The results confirm that the adaptive DT accurately replicates the dynamic response of the real-world industry-grade DiG. The DT offers a robust modeling platform for advanced MG studies that involve DiGs under multiple operation modes.

title: Experimental Assessment and Mathematical Modeling of a Self-Excited Wound Rotor Synchronous Motor With Multiphase Stator Design
abstract: Wound rotor synchronous motors (WRSMs) are emerging as a compelling alternative to permanent magnet (PM) motors in the context of electric vehicles, offering magnet-less operation and cost-effectiveness. Various techniques exist to excite the field system of synchronous motors, each presenting drawbacks. This paper investigates a self-excitation technique based on a multi-phase stator design that autonomously energizes the field winding, eliminating the need for external excitation systems or rotating transformers, thus reducing motor weight and size. The multi-phase stator generates two distinct magnetomotive force (MMF) components: a dominant flux component responsible for torque production and a harmonic component crucial for field winding excitation. Independent control of both flux components is achieved by regulating the decoupled αβ and xy sequence current components, respectively. The paper presents the mathematical modeling and steady-state equivalent circuit for this topology. Extensive testing determines the motor parameters, analyzes the relationship between xy current and field current, and examines the effects of mechanical loading and speed variations on the field current. An improved Field Oriented Control (FOC) strategy is proposed to compensate for the effects of mechanical loading due to cross-coupling between the two subspaces caused by various nonidealities. An experimental setup employing a five-phase stator is developed to validate the proposed control methodology.

title: Usage of Motor Windings as Oil Preheater for Air Conditioner Compressors
abstract: Cost optimization is a key issue for successful competition in today's home appliance markets. Therefore, many manufacturers focus on exclusion of some physical parts or circuits, which allows do decrease cost. However, in order to keep the functionality unchanged, the functions of the excluded parts are implemented using control system. This study focuses on the abovementioned direction and proposes the exclusion of the compressor oil preheater, implemented as a separate unit or circuit. In order to perform preheating, this paper proposes the usage of windings of the electrical motor, which drives the compressor and is located inside its shell. The motor windings are heated by the injected current via an inverter, and transmits the heat energy to the oil inside the compressor. Furthermore, in order to prevent motor rotation this paper recommends injection of DC current. As a result of the proposed technique, the preheater may be excluded, while the device functionality remains unchanged. The proposed manuscript analyses the pros and cons of the proposed substitution, evaluates its operation and compares it with the conventional solution.

title: Hybrid Cooling System With Water Plates and Potting for Outer-Rotor Low-Speed High-Torque PMSMs in Mining Belt Conveyors
abstract: Outer-rotor low-speed high-torque permanent magnet motors (LHPMDMs) are favored in mining belt conveyors for their simplicity and reliability, but their torque density is ultimately constrained by poor inner stator heat dissipation. To address this issue, this paper proposes a hybrid cooling method that combines axial water plate insertion with integral winding potting. This design effectively shortens the thermal conduction path from the windings to the coolant. The influence of the water plate structure on the motor’s electromagnetic performance is evaluated. A parameterized thermal network model is established for rapid optimization of the water plate position, and CFD simulations are used to optimize key parameters such as the number and thickness of the plates. Comparative analysis reveals that the proposed hybrid method reduces the winding temperature rise by 33% compared to conventional water pipe cooling. Finally, several stator modules equipped with both water plate and water pipe cooling systems are fabricated and experimentally tested, which verifies the correctness of the theoretical analysis and the feasibility of the method.

title: Online Stochastic Optimization for Coordinating EV Charging Stations With PV-Battery Systems
abstract: The surge in electric vehicle adoption strains charging stations (CSs) and the grid, calling for distributed resource integration and CS coordination to manage random supply and demand. This letter introduces a novel online stochastic optimization method that improves operation revenue and facilitates CS collaboration by ensuring the economic profitability of battery operations through a deterministic guarantee and setting battery-based prices. Simulations demonstrate near-optimal performance while upholding service quality and stability.

title: Virtual Agent and Optimal Communication Network Design for Microgrids Against DoS Attacks
abstract: The implementation of distributed secondary control makes microgrids vulnerable to denial of service (DoS) attacks on communication edges and nodes. To enhance resilience against DoS attacks and increase the survivability of real agents (RAs), this paper proposes a general and practical virtual agent (VA) framework. A lightweight VA update policy is developed and theoretically proven to be non-intrusive to normal system operation, while reducing the success rate of DoS edge and node attacks. Further, a VA-aware communication topology optimization problem is formulated to optimally connect VAs, maximizing RA survivability. Then an efficient algorithm is developed to solve the formulated problem for large-scale systems. A hardware testbed is developed with real communication protocols to replicate practical network conditions. Simulations on a 4-DG microgrid and experiments on the hardware testbed validate that the proposed method preserves normal system operation and significantly enhances resilience under DoS attacks. Additional numerical results on the IEEE 34-bus system further demonstrate the effectiveness of the optimized topology in improving RA survivability.

title: A Blockchain-Based Federated Learning Approach for Electricity Theft Detection Through Dual-Verification
abstract: Malicious clients participating in data collection and interaction may launch attacks such as model and data poisoning to degrade the performance of the global model and conceal their electricity theft behaviors. Although existing studies have introduced blockchain technology to achieve decentralization, they still suffer from limited pre-aggregation validation dimensions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a blockchain-based federated learning approach with dual-verification (BFL-DV) for electricity theft detection. In the pre-aggregation stage, a multi-metric reputation-based consensus committee verification strategy is designed, which effectively mitigates the impact of malicious participants. In the post-aggregation stage, a dynamic threshold-based blockchain verification strategy is developed to counter security risks during the transmission process, which can refuse malicious global updates adaptively. Experimental results demonstrate that BFL-DV can accurately reduce the impact of all malicious clients under the data poisoning attack. Notably, across various proportions of malicious clients, the proposed framework achieves an average AUC improvement of 32.68% compared with SOTA methods, demonstrating its consistent performance advantage.

title: Improved 3-D Hybrid Models for Open-Circuit Field Prediction in SPM Machines With Overhang Structures
abstract: This article proposes two improved 3-D hybrid models (HMs) combining subdomain (SD) and equivalent magnetic network (EMN) methods for open-circuit field prediction in two surface-mounted permanent magnet (SPM) machines with distinct overhang structures, simultaneously accounting for saturation effects and leakage flux influences. The 3-D HMs iteratively update the equivalent saturation surface current, which is used as part of the 2-D SD boundary conditions to characterize the saturation effect. The key lies in modifying the 2-D SD model to derive flux sources specific to overhang structures within the 3-D EMN model. Firstly, depending on the types of leakage flux, the machines are divided into several regions along the axial direction. Each subregion includes several slices. Then, for the PM overhang machine (POM), the flux source correction factor for each slice considering end and air-gap leakage fluxes is derived using the magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) model. Additionally, the linkage fluxes supplied by the overhang PMs are calculated and injected into the EMN units corresponding to end slices. Meanwhile, in the stator overhang machine (SOM), the axial distribution of air-gap flux density is solved using the magnetic charge model, with both leakage flux types incorporated for flux source modification. Two prototypes are fabricated, and the high accuracy and efficiency of both proposed 3-D HMs are verified by 3-D finite element analysis (FEA) and experimental results.

title: Adaptive Power Tracking and Control for Single-Stage Solar Water Pumping Systems
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive power tracking and control strategy to address the limitations of conventional voltage-based control in solar water pumping (SWP) systems. Traditional maximum power point tracking (MPPT) methods, such as Perturb and Observe (P&O) and Incremental Conductance (INC), suffer from slow convergence, oscillations, and instability under varying environmental conditions. In particular, these voltage-regulated approaches adjust load power based on photovoltaic (PV) voltage, increasing the risk of convergence to low-voltage conditions where the DC voltage becomes insufficient to sustain motor operation, resulting in excessive power loss or even system failure. To address this, an adaptive power tracking (APT) algorithm is introduced, which directly regulates power to ensure reliable operation and prevent instability. The proposed method adapts power variations based on the nonlinear voltage–current characteristics of the PV system and avoids unstable operating points without additional sensors or complex computations. Experimental results verify that the algorithm achieves fast and accurate MPPT and stable constant power control, while significantly enhancing robustness, improving system stability, and eliminating steady-state oscillations. These findings demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed approach for achieving reliable and energy-efficient SWP system operation.

title: Accurate Rotor Kinetic Energy-Based Power Smoothing Control Using Speed Increment Dynamic Compensation for PMSG-WECS
abstract: Smoothing wind power output can effectively reduce the negative impacts of wind power fluctuations on the power grid. Compared with other methods, rotor kinetic energy-based power smoothing control has the advantages of low cost and fast response. This paper proposes an accurate rotor kinetic energy-based power smoothing method using speed increment dynamic compensation for permanent magnet synchronous generator wind energy conversion systems (PMSG-WECS). Firstly, starting from the transfer function of the PMSG-WECS, the rotor kinetic energy control structure is optimized, and an accurate mathematical mapping between power and rotational speed is established. Secondly, a speed increment dynamic compensation method is designed to effectively suppress the mechanical impact of the system under critical rotational speed conditions, ensuring the operational stability while smoothing wind power fluctuations and guaranteeing wind energy utilization. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed novel power smoothing control method are verified through the establishment of the simulation model and construction of an experimental platform.

title: Analytical Model for Predicting Rotor Eddy Current Loss of PMSMs Considering Magnetic Saturation and Diffusion Effect
abstract: Rotor eddy-current loss (RECL) in permanent-magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) is strongly influenced by magnetic core saturation and diffusion effect (eddy-current reaction) in conducting parts. Many analytical models omit one of these, leading to errors at high load or under rich harmonics. This paper proposes a nonlinear hybrid analytical framework that couples a magnetostatic model (MSM) with a frequency-domain model (FDM) via an equivalent current-sheet (ECS) interface. The MSM computes the load-dependent magnetic field under nonlinear core permeability. Over one electrical period, the tangential field at the inner stator surface is sampled and decomposed by fast Fourier transform (FFT) into ECSs with explicit space-time orders. These ECSs are subsequently fed to the FDM, which solves the diffusion problem in conductive rotor regions, yielding per-harmonic RECL estimates. Compared with 2D finite-element analysis (FEA), the method maintains high accuracy across saturation levels and frequencies while requiring substantially lower computational effort. Experimental validation is carried out on a PMSM using a thermal-based method to infer rotor losses. The proposed model using a 3D correction shows good agreement with the test results. This model provides a transparent loss mechanism and is suitable for early-stage design studies where both saturation and diffusion are significant.

title: Synergistic Dual-Mechanism Self-Powered Photodetector with Broadband Polarization Sensitivity for Multifunctional Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) photodetectors are a research focus in optoelectronics owing to their excellent flexibility and integration. However, conventional 2D photodetectors typically rely on a single photoresponse mechanism, and studies on synergizing multiple physical mechanisms to enhance detection performance remain insufficient. Herein, we demonstrate a high-performance self-powered Gr/InSe/MoS2 van der Waals heterojunction photodetector with a unilateral depletion n-n junction. By rationally integrating graphene, InSe, and MoS2, the device realizes remarkable synergistic enhancement by dual-mechanism of photovoltaic and photothermoelectric effects. Benefiting from the thermoelectric field induced by the temperature gradient in MoS2 aligns with the built-in field of the n-n junction, effectively promote efficient photocarrier separation and significantly improving the photoresponse. Under zero-bias operation, it exhibits a broadband photoresponse from 355 to 1064 nm, a peak responsivity of 650 mA W−1 at 532 nm, an ultralow dark current of 5.3 × 10−13 A, and a fast rise time of 15.6 μs. Meanwhile, the device displays distinct polarization sensitivity originating from the in-plane anisotropy of InSe. It is successfully applied to image encryption, polarization imaging, and near-infrared optical communication, providing a promising strategy for designing advanced multifunctional self-powered photodetectors.

title: Regulating Surface Chemistry and Interfacial Kinetics of Ni-Rich NCM Cathodes via a Polyaniline-Derived Interphase
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ni-rich LiNixCoyMn1-x-yO2 cathodes (NCM, Ni ≥ 80%) are promising for high-energy lithium-ion batteries, but their practical use is constrained by surface instability, interfacial side reactions, and sluggish charge-transfer kinetics during cycling. Herein, a conductive interphase derived from polyaniline (PANI) was constructed on LiNi0.9Co0.05Mn0.05O2 (NCM90) through a facile solution-assisted coating strategy. The optimized NCM90@PANI preserves the layered structure and particle morphology of NCM90 while forming a thin and continuous PANI-containing surface layer. Benefiting from this interfacial modification, NCM90@PANI exhibits enhanced cycling stability, improved rate capability, and better air-storage stability than pristine NCM90. The improvement is attributed to the protective and kinetically favorable interphase, which reduces interfacial polarization, maintains favorable Li+ transport kinetics, suppresses continuous electrolyte decomposition, and mitigates the accumulation of resistive surface byproducts. The PANI-containing interphase also reduces H2O/CO2-induced surface degradation during air storage. Diffusion-stress simulation further qualitatively illustrates that improved interfacial flux uniformity can promote a more homogeneous Li distribution and alleviate localized stress concentration. This work demonstrates that PANI-derived interphase engineering provides an effective strategy for simultaneously regulating the surface chemistry and interfacial kinetics of Ni-rich NCM cathodes.

title: HfO2 Nanocrystal-Reinforced Flexible SiC Nanofibrous Membranes with Excellent Cyclic Bending Durability and Thermal Insulation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Flexible HfO2/SiC composite nanofibrous membranes were fabricated via a polymer-derived ceramic strategy by incorporating HfO2 nanocrystals into a SiC matrix. The optimized membrane exhibits a tensile strength of 1.97 MPa, a static load-bearing capability of approximately 3800 times its own weight, and excellent cyclic bending durability, maintaining ΔR/R0 below 3% after 1.6 × 104 cycles under 180° repeated bending. These results demonstrate its robust mechanical stability under both static loading and repeated bending deformation. Concurrently, the membrane achieves a low thermal conductivity of 0.1513 W·m−1·K−1 and a high infrared emissivity of ∼0.95. When subjected to direct exposure to a 1200 °C flame, a 2.5 mm-thick membrane exhibits a backside temperature of only 172.6 °C. The measured temperature-difference sustainability per unit thickness is 1.19 × 105 °C·s·mm−1 under prolonged thermal exposure, which is 1.6 times that of conventional ceramic, fibrous, and aerogel insulators. Moreover, molecular dynamics simulations provide further evidence that the incorporation of HfO2 has a reinforcing effect. These results highlight the potential of HfO2/SiC nanofibrous membranes for lightweight thermal protection applications under extreme environments.

title: Flexible Red Quantum Dot Light-Emitting Diodes Enabled by a Highly Conductive and Transparent Poly(benzodifurandione) Electrode
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract As a highly conductive polymer, poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) shows great potential in flexible electrodes. Yet its poor interfacial compatibility with the traditional hole-transport layer PEDOT:PSS limits device performance, posing a key challenge for practical applications. To address this issue, we developed a novel oil-soluble hole-transport system comprising PF8Cz-TPA doped with TrTPFB. TrTPFB p-type doping boosts PF8Cz-TPA's hole transport and work-function matching, enabling its single layer to replace the PEDOT:PSS/PF8Cz-TPA bilayer, improving device performance and simplifying manufacturing. The optimized PBFDO-based red quantum dot light-emitting diode (QLED) delivers exceptional performance: a low turn-on voltage of 1.9 V, a maximum luminance of 39,603 cd m–2, and a peak current efficiency of 15.15 cd A–1. This peak efficiency is about four times that of undoped devices (3.92 cd A–1) and reaches 79% of the performance of ITO-based devices. PBFDO-based devices exhibited superior operational stability, with luminance dropping from 19,000 to 12,000 cd m–2 over 120 h, while ITO-based devices degraded rapidly, falling from 12,000 to 5000 cd m–2 in just 45 h. Flexible QLEDs built on PEN substrates deliver a current efficiency of 10.96 cd A–1, confirming their promising prospects in flexible display technologies.

title: Fibrous Intrinsic Zeolitic Pickering Interfacial Catalysts
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Previously, our research group reported the preparation of stable Pickering emulsions using a zeolite with intrinsic amphiphilicity that required no surface grafting. Nevertheless, although the emulsification capability was intrinsic, the catalytic active sites (Pd metal nanoclusters) remained “extrinsic”. In the present study, we successfully achieved both intrinsic emulsification and intrinsic catalysis using pristine MTT zeolite. The high anisotropy (anisotropy index = 23.2) and excellent dispersibility endowed the zeolite with favorable emulsifying performance, enabling the unmodified zeolite to effectively stabilize Pickering emulsions. Remarkably, Brønsted acid sites are naturally present in pristine raw-MTT zeolite. Therefore, we successfully realized the integration of both intrinsic emulsification and intrinsic catalytic functionality within the same zeolitic material, greatly simplifying catalyst design. We constructed a Pickering interfacial catalytic system using fibrous MTT zeolite for epoxide hydration ring opening. The catalyst affords nearly quantitative substrate conversion (99.9%) within 20 min, along with a turnover frequency (TOF) of 70 h–1. Furthermore, the MTT zeolite preserves considerable catalytic activity and high recovery efficiency over five successive reaction cycles.

title: A Multi-Objective Global Optimization Method for Linear-Rotary PMSM Using an Improved Kriging Model
abstract: To address the challenges of quick optimization of linear-rotary permanent magnet synchronous motor (LRPMSM) due to complicate two-degree-of-freedom(2-DoF) structure, this paper proposes a multi-objective global optimization method with Kriging-assistance. First, the topology structure of LRPMSM is introduced, and a global optimization method based on parameter layering is proposed. By sensitivity analysis, the 9 parameters are stratified into three subspaces. Low-sensitivity 3 parameters are optimized via finite element analysis (FEA) or assigned fixed values, reducing optimization variables by 33.33%. For remaining 6 highly sensitive key parameters, an improved Kriging model is developed, integrating adaptive kernel function selection and Bayesian optimization. With only 400 samples, the accurate surrogate model is obtained, and then the optimization is performed by adopting multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO). Based on the optimized design, the no-load back-EMF and detent force are measured, which are consistent with the predicted results. Experimental results on a prototype confirm the accuracy of the predictions, demonstrating that the proposed method is a fast and effective global optimization framework for complex multi-DoF motors.

title: Thermal-Mechanical Unified Inertia Estimation and Enhancement of Free Piston Stirling Generator in Island Microgrid
abstract: Compared with power electronic converter and diesel generator, the free piston Stirling generator (FPSG) with maintenance-free features has many advantages such as large overcurrent capability, high reliability, and wide heat source adaptability, as well as providing voltage and frequency references. Therefore, FPSG is a powerful competitor in supplying power to island microgrids and providing inertia to resist disturbance. However, unlike rotating devices, FPSG is a thermal-mechanical coupled system, and the two sets of vibrating components are subjected to approximate sinusoidal harmonic vibration, which poses difficulties for inertia analysis. To fill this gap, this paper provides a method for accurately calculating the frequency and power response during the dynamic process, which is the core of inertia analysis. Subsequently, a unified thermal-mechanical inertia estimation method that considers both the frequency reduction to provide mechanical power and the displacement of pistons increase to convert more thermal power is proposed. Then, the inertia enhancement method is provided, which effectively increases the frequency nadir and transition time. Finally, the proposed inertia estimation and enhancement method is verified through simulation and experiment.

title: Adaptive Pump Fault Detection for Vanadium Redox Flow Batteries Based on CNN-BiGRU and Transfer Learning
abstract: Vanadium redox flow batteries (VRBs) are vulnerable to pump malfunctions, which can cause severe problems like overcharging, overdischarging, and irreversible damage to the battery stack. Effective real-time fault detection methods for VRBs are essential but underdeveloped. This study proposes a data-driven approach for VRB pump fault detection using a convolutional neural network combined with bi-directional gated recurrent units to predict voltage based on measurable current, flow rate, and state of charge without relying on complex electrochemical models. To address the impact of battery aging and system variability, which are often overlooked in the literature, an offline transfer learning strategy with model tail fine-tuning is employed to adapt the parameters of the pre-trained model using a small amount of newly collected data. Pump faults are identified by comparing voltage prediction errors against a threshold derived from the 3σ criterion. Experimental results across six fault scenarios encompassing three distinct pump fault modes under two operational conditions demonstrate that the proposed method achieves timely and accurate fault detection, significantly improving the reliability of VRB systems.

title: Field Current Estimation for Brushless Wound-Field Synchronous Machine Equipped With Synchronous Exciter
abstract: Owing to the high reliability and low maintenance requirement, brushless synchronous generators (BLSG) are used in many applications from small power generating sets to large-capacity turbo-generators. In BLSG, direct measurement of the field current and its voltage is normally not possible. Consequently, accurate estimation of these quantities is essential for condition monitoring, state and parameter estimation, control and protection purposes. In this paper, a new method based on extended Kalman filter with unknown input (EKF-UI) is proposed for estimation of field current. This method which considers the field voltage as an unknown input is used for field current estimation in BLSG equipped with synchronous excitation system. The proposed method is validated by several case studies, including open loop and closed loop control systems and rotating rectifier faults. The experimental and simulation results show that, using the proposed method, the field current can be accurately estimated in both steady states and transients.

title: Low Copper Loss High-Resistance Connection Fault Tolerant Method in Five-Phase PMSM With Current and Voltage Reconfiguration
abstract: The high-resistance connection (HRC) fault in the five-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) leads to increased copper losses and reduced efficiency due to impedance imbalance. The impedance model under HRC fault is incorporated into the proposed fault-tolerant control method. A current and voltage reconfiguration is also adopted with the constraint of minimizing copper loss (MCL). Additionally, the maximization of torque output range with low copper loss (MTMCL) constraint is also proposed for more torque output capability. Combined with the above two constraints and proposed fault tolerant control method, a fault tolerant coefficient switching strategy following electromagnetic torque is also summarized for minimization copper loss without overheating. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed control method achieves a significant reduction in copper loss compared to original method.

title: Additional AC Copper Losses in the Field Winding of Converter-Fed Synchronous Machines for Pumped Storage Hydropower Plants
abstract: Converter-fed synchronous machines for variable speed pumped storage hydropower plants are becoming increasingly important as the share of fluctuating renewable energy increases. The inverter connected to the stator terminals causes additional harmonic currents in the stator winding, which induce additional harmonic currents in the field winding. Due to the eddy current effects and the typical form-wound coil design, these additional harmonic currents in the field winding can lead to significant additional losses, even with relatively small amplitudes. The aim of this paper is to calculate these additional losses. Therefore, numerical calculations are used to determine the resistance factor for a frequency band from $\text{0}\,\text{Hz}$ to $\text{15}\,\text{kHz}$ while also considering saturation. In addition, two measurements are carried out on a research hydro generator at different inverter switching frequencies. Using the measured currents and determined resistance factors, the additional losses due to the switching frequency are calculated and validated using a temperature measurement in the field winding. The results of this work are important for the future design and cooling of large converter-fed synchronous machines with form-wound field coils, as the additional AC losses in the field winding are usually neglected.

title: Sensorless Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Using Model Predictive Algorithm Based Back-EMF Observer
abstract: Back-electromotive force (back-EMF) based sensorless control is widely applied in permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drives. For high-gain back-EMF observers, the control law often leads to an inherent trade-off between steady-state accuracy and dynamic response. To address this issue, a model predictive control (MPC)-based observer designed in discrete-time domain is proposed in this article. In the studied observer, the optimal control action selected from a predetermined set is adopted to eliminate the current estimation error. Then, the estimated back-EMFs can be extracted from the applied control actions. By leveraging traversing optimization, the proposed method improves the current error and observation accuracy while maintaining fast response and robustness. Experimental results conducted on a 1-kW PMSM platform verify the effectiveness of the proposed observer.

title: Dynamic Current Control Strategy of Grid-Connected Voltage Source Converters Feeding Constant Power Loads for Transient Stability Enhancement
abstract: The negative impedance characteristic of constant power loads (CPLs) can destabilize grid-connected voltage source converters (VSCs) by introducing positive feedback loops. To this end, this paper proposes a dynamic current control strategy for grid-connected VSCs with CPLs to enhance system transient synchronous stability (TSS). Firstly, a nonlinear phase-locked loop dynamic model is developed for VSCs. It explicitly incorporates the CPL impact, which indicates CPLs introduce coupling between the d-axis and q-axis components of VSC terminal voltage, and a positive feedback loop in VSC control scheme. Secondly, equal area criterion and phase-portrait analysis are used for qualitative and quantitative analysis to assess the CPL impact on TSS, respectively. The findings indicate the impact is related to the VSC output current. Therefore, a dynamic current control strategy for VSCs is proposed. It adds the current compensation term to neutralize CPL-induced destabilizing effects, guaranteeing the existence of stable equilibrium points that ensure both TSS and CPLs operation at rated power under grid faults. Meanwhile, a simple and fast VSC capacity calculation method is proposed. It can accurately calculate the required VSC capacity for achieving the above control objectives. Finally, simulation and experimental comparisons with existing methods verify the validity of the proposed strategy.

title: A Precise Nonlinear Eddy-Current Magnetic Network Model for the Analysis of Electromagnetic Buffer
abstract: In this paper, a precise nonlinear eddy-current magnetic network (PNEMN) model is proposed to analyze the performance of the cylindrical permanent magnet (PM) electromagnetic buffer (EB). In this EB, the permanent magnet is radially magnetized and separated by iron teeth. When the EB is working, intense eddy currents are induced, severely distorting the original magnetic field, so that conventional magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) models can no longer provide an accurate solution. To solve this problem, this paper adopted refined magnetic reluctance elements and incorporated eddy currents into the magnetic network model, fully coupling them with the original magnetic field. The convergence of this method is discussed in detail. To make this model more comprehensive, nonlinear magnetic saturation, end effects, and slot effects have also been taken into account. Optimal computational efficiency is achieved by judiciously selecting boundary conditions. A finite element model and the experiments on a prototype were built to verify the accuracy of the proposed model. Finally, the operating characteristics of the eddy current brake are analyzed, and its critical speed is about 7.5 m/s.

title: Sliding-Mode Speed Control for Predictive-Torque-Control-Based Induction-Machine Drives Based on Adaptive-Variable-Rate Reaching Law and Disturbance-Extended Sliding-Mode Observer
abstract: For the predictive-torque-control (PTC) based induction-machine (IM) drives, to promote the speed tracking performance as well as the robustness against various unknown disturbances, such as friction, external load disturbance and parameter mismatch. A sliding-mode control with adaptive-variable-rate reaching law (SMC-AVRRL) and a disturbance-extended sliding-mode observer (DESMO) is proposed. First, the speed loop of PTC which utilizes the classical PI control is analyzed. It indicates that the control performance of the PI controller degrades apparently under sudden load disturbances and induction-machine parameters mismatch. Then the sliding-mode control with adaptive-variable-rate reaching law is proposed. Taking the typical reaching law, namely exponential reaching law (ERL), as a comparison object, the AVRRL method can reduce the chattering and convergence time simultaneously. The stability of the proposed SMC-AVRRL is analyzed by the Lyapunov stability theory. Moreover, to further enhance the anti-disturbance capacity, the proposed SMC-AVRRL is then combined with a disturbance-extended sliding-mode observer (DESMO), named the SMC-AVRRL + DESMO method. The experimental results show that the proposed SMC-AVRRL + DESMO method can not only achieve high speed tracking accuracy, but also achieves better robustness.

title: Pricing Appliance Usage Privacy for Enhancing Usability of Smart Meter Data
abstract: Consumers’ privacy concerns often limit the usage of their smart meter data in several data-driven applications. While privacy-preserving algorithms can address the privacy concerns of consumers, these algorithms erase useful information; thus reducing the data usability. Data usability can be enhanced if the utility can directly utilize the smart meter data of consumers without transforming the same using privacy-preserving algorithms. However, this is not possible unless consumers give up their privacy rights over their smart meter data. Offering monetary compensations to consumers can be a possible approach to encourage them to give up the privacy rights over their smart meter data. Hence, this paper proposes a novel privacy pricing method that monetarily compensates the loss of appliance usage privacy incurred by the consumers who agreed to give up the privacy rights over their smart meter data. At first, a consumer’s appliance usage privacy is modeled based on how the consumer’s consumptions fluctuate over a given time period. Then, a nonlinear convex optimization problem is proposed using the privacy model to determine the privacy prices of a set of consumers under a given budget of the utility. The properties of the optimal solution are demonstrated mathematically. It is shown that the practical implementation of the proposed pricing method is unlikely to impact the consumption patterns of consumers. The impacts of the utility’s budget and the number of participating consumers on the privacy prices are illustrated using practical smart meter data while considering heterogeneity in the privacy concerns of consumers. Further, a novel metric is proposed which shows that, unlike the existing pricing methods, the privacy prices generated by the proposed method are sufficient to address the privacy concerns of most of the participating consumers.

title: A Novel Magnetic Integrated Three-Phase EMI Filter for Differential-Mode and Common-Mode Interference Suppression in PMSM Drive Systems
abstract: The application of three-phase electromagnetic interference (EMI) filters in permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive systems can reduce common-mode (CM) interference while filtering out differential-mode (DM) interference in phase currents. Conventional filters will increase the volume and weight of the system. This article proposes a fully magnetic integrated three-phase EMI filter, with a magnetic core consisting of a toroid and a Y-branch limb. The toroid is primarily employed to concentrate the CM flux while providing the path for the DM flux. The Y-branch limb is used to carry the DM flux. The distribution of the flux in the proposed filter under different winding distribution patterns is analyzed. The DM and CM inductances are derived. The optimal winding distribution pattern is determined through quantitative and qualitative comparison. The magnetic saturation analysis is provided by deriving the maximum magnetic flux density of the proposed filter. The magnetic flux density of the proposed filter is verified through ANSYS simulation. The experiment is conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed filter. The results show that the proposed filter can significantly reduce the volume and weight of the system compared to the conventional filter under the same DM and CM suppression performance. In addition, a DC side EMI filter is manufactured to assess its impact on the electrical performance of the motor side. The results indicate that the DC side EMI filter cannot replace the proposed filter. The proposed filter can enhance the performance and reliability of the PMSM drive system.

title: Physics-Informed Series-Aware Graph Transformer Model for Net Load Forecasting
abstract: The growing integration of renewable energy sources (RESs), such as photovoltaic (PV) and wind (WD), has significantly increased the variability of net load (NL), posing critical challenges on the net load forecasting. In this paper, a novel physics-informed series-aware graph Transformer (PISAGT) model is proposed for the net load forecasting, which synergistically combines the advantages of both direct and indirect forecasting methods to achieve superior forecasting performance. Firstly, a physics-informed loss module (PILM) is proposed, which introduces the physical characteristics of the net load into the loss function to incorporate physical knowledge in the gradient descent optimization, thereby enhancing the model’s generalization capability for more stable and trustworthy predictions. Secondly, a variable-scale patch embedding method segments time series into subsequence-level patches and transforms them into 2D representations, which enables the forecast model to simultaneously capture local temporal patterns across diverse forecasting horizons. Thirdly, a series-aware graph learning mechanism (SAGLM) which includes graph token encoding, adaptive adjacency matrix learning, and graph convolution, is proposed to integrate graph neural networks (GNNs) with Transformer within a synergistic framework to comprehensively capture intra-series and inter-series dependencies in net load datasets. Finally, case studies on the real-world datasets demonstrate that the PISAGT model can achieve a 14.4% improvement in prediction accuracy compared with direct forecasting methods, showing its effectiveness in net load forecasting.

title: Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Control Based on Model-Free Predictive Current Control for PMSM With Dual Star-Delta Windings
abstract: This paper proposes a model-free predictive current control combined with an adaptive fault-tolerant control (AFTC-MFPCC) strategy for dual star-delta windings permanent magnet synchronous motor (DSDW-PMSM) under different phase shift angles. The proposed strategy enhances the operational performance of this motor when current sensor fault or open-phase fault occur in any star-connected winding phase, showing strong adaptability and robustness. Firstly, the invariance of the fundamental magnetomotive force (MMF) under single open-phase fault in DSDW-PMSM with different phase shift angles is analytically derived. Secondly, an adaptive fault-tolerant control strategy is proposed. Upon detecting a persistent zero current in any phase, it switches the adaptive fault-tolerant transformation matrix without explicit fault diagnosis, thereby avoiding the impact of current sensor faults and reducing the fault detection time. Subsequently, the xy-axis reference values are modified through current feedback, enabling the motor to adaptively transition from the fault state to the normal operation state. Furthermore, model-free predictive current control is employed to replace traditional PI control or deadbeat predictive current control in the current loop module of the vector control structure, which outputs four voltage vectors. This method avoids current tracking errors and severe waveform distortion caused by inaccuracies in motor parameter inputs. Finally, tests are conducted on a 24-slot/10-pole DSDW-PMSM with a 15° phase shift to validate the feasibility of the proposed method.

title: Real-Time Reactive Power Limits of Synchronous Generators: Application to the New Spanish Voltage Control System
abstract: The voltage control of the Spanish transmission network faces growing challenges due to the high penetration of renewable energy sources, as evidenced by the Iberian Peninsula blackout on April 28, 2025. Synchronous generators have traditionally ensured voltage stability, but their role becomes even more critical in low-inertia systems with limited synchronous generation. This paper presents a real-time method for computing the reactive power limits of synchronous generators at the network connection point, aligned with the new Spanish voltage control system. The proposed approach determines maximum and minimum reactive power capabilities as functions of active power, network voltage, transformer tap position, and key generator constraints, including armature current, excitation system and stability limits, and admissible voltage ranges. Unlike the conventional p–q representation used by manufacturers, European transmission system operators now define reactive power requirements in the q–v plane. The method reflects this shift by computing and displaying reactive limits in the q–v plane to ensure compliance. The approach is validated with a field test of a 213 MVA hydropower plant, and a simulation test of a 450 MVA single-shaft combined-cycle gas turbine, with sensitivity analyses exploring the impact of key parameters on q–v compliance. Time-domain simulations demonstrate how reactive power limits evolve dynamically in response to changing operating conditions, supporting more accurate and robust voltage control in real time.

title: Improved Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control With Disturbance Observer for Five-Phase Fault-Tolerant IPM Motor Drives
abstract: This paper presents a composite control strategy for five-phase fault-tolerant fractional-slot concentrated winding interior permanent magnet (FTFSCW-IPM) motor drives, aiming to alleviate the long-standing trade-off between fast dynamic response, chattering suppression, and disturbance rejection in sliding mode control. A variable exponential fast terminal reaching law with a continuous switching function is developed to explicitly shape the reaching dynamics, enabling rapid convergence when the system state is far from the sliding surface while ensuring smooth behavior near the surface. To further enhance robustness against load torque disturbances, a Luenberger torque disturbance observer (LTDO) with a slightly enhanced correction structure is incorporated as a feedforward compensation channel, thereby decoupling disturbance rejection from the sliding-mode switching gain design. In addition, a systematic comparative study involving four representative control schemes is conducted to clearly distinguish the individual and combined effects of the fast terminal sliding mode structure and the disturbance observer. Both simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy achieves excellent speed tracking performance and improved disturbance rejection under sudden load torque variations.

title: Transfer Learning for Data-Efficient Magnetic Core Loss Modeling in Electrical Machines via Parametric Homogenization and Neural Networks
abstract: Despite the urgent demand in industry, there do not yet exist practical and accurate simulation methods for calculating the magnetic losses of ferromagnetic laminated cores in electrical machine (EM) simulations. Transfer learning, a machine learning technique, utilizes a model developed for one task as a starting point for developing a model for another task. This study innovatively integrates parametric homogenized material laws with deep learning (DL) approaches. Firstly, the intrinsic resistance parameters characterizing core material properties are investigated through the combined application of the Bertotti model and an improved equivalent circuit model. Experimental data from prototypes are then used to visualize the influence patterns of different temperatures, harmonics, loads, and frequencies on these derived parameters. To both reduce the required data for improved performance and model the underlying mechanisms of mutual parameter impact, a sizeable auxiliary dataset was synthetically generated through the synergistic application of support vector machine, decision tree, and backpropagation (BP) neural network algorithms. By leveraging the pre-learned patterns of parameter variation, auxiliary data, and a small set of target data covering high-frequency, high-temperature, and high-load conditions, a two-stage feature transfer learning process is implemented using deep sparse autoencoder and BP neural network. Finally, comparative experiments are designed to verify the limitations of existing loss evaluation methods and to emphasize the importance of comprehensively considering multi-factor coupling effects in EM core loss modeling. The results demonstrate that the proposed local material law can serve as a conventional constitutive relationship in two-dimensional or three-dimensional modeling, and, when combined with DL algorithms, achieves a massive speed-up compared to monolithic coupling.

title: Radial Displacement Sensorless Control of Permanent Magnet Assisted Bearingless Synchronous Reluctance Motor in Full Speed Range
abstract: The displacement sensors utilized in the control system of the permanent magnet assisted bearingless synchronous reluctance motor (PMa-BSynRM) are associated with high cost and low reliability. To address this, this paper proposes a radial displacement sensorless control method in the full speed range. Firstly, the rotor suspension principle is expounded, and the voltage and current equations of the system are derived. Secondly, in the low speed range, the rotor displacement is estimated using high frequency square wave injection (HFSWI) combined with a phase-locked loop (PLL) for accurate signal demodulation. Thirdly, a left inverse observer is constructed using an improved radial basis function (RBF) neural network, and the initial parameters of the neural network are optimized by the weighted mean of vectors algorithm (INFO), ultimately achieving accurate displacement estimation. Furthermore, the transition boundaries between operational modes are determined through deceleration simulation, incorporating a weighted fusion algorithm to guarantee seamless switching across speed regions. Finally, the proposed approach is verified through simulation and comparative experiments. Experimental results demonstrate a maximum steady-state estimation error of 7 μm, while the settling time extends by only 11 ms under external disturbances. Overall, the proposed method exhibits superior estimation precision and robust disturbance rejection capability.

title: Research on Analytical Method of Parasitic Capacitance in Motor Windings Considering Impact of Distributed Disorder
abstract: The equivalent parasitic capacitance (Cp) of motor windings causes the voltage/current overshoot and ringing during the switching of wide-bandgap semiconductor devices. Therefore, it is necessary to model and calculate Cp to evaluate its impact on the switching devices. However, due to the winding deviations and spatial constraints of the slots, the arrangement of coils is disordered. Using the ideal single value of Cp may lead to the significant deviations in the evaluation of switching transients. To address the above issues, the analytical method of parasitic capacitance considering the impact of distributed disorder is studied in this paper. The impact of the winding model on the calculated value of Cp is investigated. The winding distribution patterns are categorized into three types: uniform, partially disordered, and fully disordered. An analytical method for the distributed capacitance is developed, incorporating the influence of random coil placement.
