A set of samples for the parasitic capacitance values of disordered windings is generated using a random sampling method. The sample distribution is determined through confidence intervals and the Chernoff bound to approximate the original distribution. The similarity between the two distributions is verified using the K-S test. The region with the highest frequency in the sample distribution is identified as the prediction interval for the winding’s parasitic capacitance value. Finally, the measurements are performed on the disordered distribution winding samples. The results prove the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

title: Nonlinear Loss-Minimizing Control of Induction Motors With Inherent Constraint Satisfaction
abstract: In this paper, a novel nonlinear loss-minimizing control structure is proposed for induction motors that achieves field-oriented operation and minimization of the total copper and iron motor losses at the steady state, while inherently guaranteeing the required operating constraints (current and voltage). Opposed to the conventional loss-minimizing controllers that require the solution of a complex optimization problem and the continuous (online) update of the current reference values depending on the operating constraints, the proposed nonlinear loss-minimizing control (NLMC) introduces a novel structure that inherently limits the motor current and voltage inside the desired constraint set and requires the solution of a simplified optimization problem offline. Using nonlinear system theory (ultimate boundedness, vector field and invariant set theory), the boundedness of the motor currents and the entire constraint satisfaction are analytically proven for the proposed NLMC application, followed by a detailed closed-loop system stability analysis. In order to verify the theoretical contribution, the proposed NLMC is directly compared to the well-established field-oriented control and the conventional loss-minimizing control, using a digital Typhoon HIL real-time simulator and an experimental setup of a 1.5 kW Leroy Somer induction motor with varying speed reference and load torque values. Both the real-time simulation and the experimental procedure prove the NLMC capability of regulating the motor speed under speed reference values and torque load changes, while it achieves a minimum losses operation with inherent constraints satisfaction, by utilizing a simpler optimization problem.

title: A Novel Modified Logistic Function Based PV Source Modeling for PV Power Applications
abstract: In this paper, a novel modified logistic function-based explicit model for PV modules is proposed for accurate modeling of PV modules with minimal current-voltage (I<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$-$</tex-math></inline-formula>V) curve data points. The proposed model requires only three I<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$-$</tex-math></inline-formula>V coordinates: open circuit voltage, short circuit current, and maximum power points provided by the manufacturer or obtained experimentally. The shape parameters of the proposed model are calculated using a newly derived simplified expression based on hyperbolic identities. Therefore, the proposed model significantly reduces the computational complexity compared to the conventional benchmarks, such as implicit single diode and double diode models of PV module. The proposed model is validated for various PV modules of different cell types of technologies under different environmental conditions in terms of % error in maximum power point. The method eliminates the complex calculations, dependence on several PV parameters and the laboratory-based analysis of solar modules.

title: Battery Storage in More- and All-Electric Fishing Vessels: Real-Time Simulation and Experimental Verification
abstract: The transition of fuel-reliant fishing vessels to more- and all-electric alternatives is essential to reduce the fishing industry’s dependence on fuel. Most research on the energy transition in the maritime industry has focused on larger vessels. Larger vessels typically have multiple generation units; however, fishing vessels have fewer onboard resources, making control and operation more challenging. This paper introduces the development of a real-time simulation testbed for small fishing vessels using two Typhoon HIL 604 real-time simulators. Data obtained from an actual purse seine fishing vessel are applied in developing, validating, and benchmarking models for vessel dynamics, propeller behavior, and hydraulic performance. The models are adaptable and represent a 58-foot fishing vessel, including its propulsion system, hydraulic load, and battery storage capable of operating in both grid-forming and grid-following modes. The testbed is then used to examine integration of a battery energy storage system (BESS): during transit, during fishing operations, and during both transit and fishing operations. The results demonstrate the distinct benefits of both small and large battery installations on fishing vessels, including shorter travel time between the harbor and fishing grounds, stable voltage and frequency across operating modes, and reduced noise during fishing operations.

title: Impact of Shielding Configurations With Magnetic-Electrically Conductive Alloy on Multi-Physical Fields in the End Region of Air-Cooled Synchronous Condenser
abstract: In large-capacity air-cooled synchronous condensers (ACSCs) operating under deep leading-phase conditions, significant end leakage flux induces substantial losses and heating in the stator end components. Effective electromagnetic shielding is therefore a critical design consideration and a novel shielding configuration utilizing magnetic-electrical conductive alloys is proposed in this article. Using a 300 MVar ACSC as a case study, the three-dimensional transient electromagnetic field model of the end region is first established. The effects of four configurations (copper shield+magnetic shield, Fe-16<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\%$</tex-math></inline-formula>Cu alloy shield+magnetic shield, single Fe-20<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\%$</tex-math></inline-formula>Cu alloy shield, and single magnetic shield) on the leakage flux density and losses in end components are analyzed. Subsequently, a global ventilation network and a fluid-thermal coupling model for the end region are developed for each configuration. The results from network and aforementioned losses serve as boundary conditions for the fluid-thermal coupling model. The flow fields and the temperature distributions under different configurations are then determined. The findings demonstrate that each shielding configuration exhibits specific advantages and limitations. Experimental validation based on traditional scheme confirms the accuracy of the model and methodology. The simulation results elucidate the significant potential of the Fe-Cu alloy. The single Fe-20<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\%$</tex-math></inline-formula>Cu configuration reduces the hot-spot temperature of shield, and significantly lowers weight and cost while effectively protecting the end iron core.

title: Analysis and Calculation of the Control Winding Current During Crowbarless Asymmetrical Low-Voltage Ride-Through for Brushless Doubly-Fed Induction Generators
abstract: The present control winding (CW) current calculations are inaccurate due to the incomplete consideration of the output limitation of the machine side converter (MSC) during the crowbarless asymmetrical low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) of the brushless doubly-fed induction generator (BDFIG). Furthermore, there is a paucity of literature on the relationship between the peak CW currents and the time of the fault occurrence, which has a distinct impact on the analysis and evaluation of the effectiveness of the BDFIG LVRT control strategy. To address this challenge, this paper considers the transient process in the MSC, provides an innovative approximate expression for the CW flux linkage in SVPWM overmodulation, and derives an expression for the CW transient current considering the time of fault occurrence for the first time. From the expression, the CW current of the BDFIG prototype was calculated when the fault occurs at different moments. The calculation results indicate that the peak value of CW is closely related to the time of the fault occurrence and the maximum peak value of the CW current is more than twice the minimum peak value when the fault occurs at different times. Extensive simulation and experimental results under different asymmetrical short-circuit fault have validated the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed expression.

title: Stage-Wise Analytical Modeling of the Stray Magnetic Field in Surface-Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Under Mixed Eccentricity
abstract: Conventional subdomain methods face challenges in calculating the stray magnetic field of surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motors (SPMSMs) under eccentric conditions due to their inability to handle complex boundaries, leading to low computational efficiency. To address these issues, this paper proposes a cell-based Schwarz-Christoffel (SC) mapping method and a stage-wise calculation strategy to improve computational efficiency while maintaining accuracy. First, an analytical model (AM) integrating equivalent surface current, conformal transformation method is established. Based on magnetic field superposition, the load air-gap magnetic field is derived. Second, a stage-wise subdomain-based computational strategy is employed to decouple the magnetic field calculations for the air-gap region and the outer air region. The stray magnetic field is analytically modeled using SC mapping and separation of variables. Finally, the proposed method is validated through experiments on an 8-pole 18-slot interior-rotor SPMSM with mixed eccentricity. Results show that the TM achieves a computational error of only 3.49% and that the computational speed is 136 times faster than that of the finite element method (FEM).

title: Multi-Stress Aging of Service-Aged and Backup Hydrogenerator Stator Coils Under Load Cycling
abstract: Frequent start–stops in hydrogenerators impose increased thermal, mechanical, and electrical stresses on stator winding insulation, accelerating degradation and potentially leading to failure. To emulate such operating conditions, a multi-stress, single-phase stator-slot model was built to cycle stator coils between 40 and 110 <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^{\circ }$</tex-math></inline-formula>C while simultaneously applying 1.5 times the rated phase-to-ground voltage (<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${U_{0}}$</tex-math></inline-formula>). Service-aged and backup coil groups taken from the same hydrogenerator were tested, with partial discharge (PD) recorded during cycling (on-cycle) and off-cycle diagnostics at room temperature, including PD inception voltage, PD measurements at 1.5 <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$U_{0}$</tex-math></inline-formula>, and loss tangent. The on-cycle results show distinct aging trajectories: the service-aged coils entered a stable-degradation regime with limited, similar discharge magnitudes during heating and cooling, whereas the backup coils exhibited larger, more frequent discharges, with PD markedly higher during cooling than during heating at the same temperature. Off-cycle measurements indicate similar trends but with lower magnitudes, suggesting that room-temperature tests alone cannot probe multi-stress degradation. The study demonstrates that reliable assessment requires the use of combined on-cycle and off-cycle diagnostics under representative loading conditions.

title: Spatial-Constrained Structure Optimization of the Mover for Minimizing Power Consumption in Maglev Planar Motors
abstract: This paper presents a novel spatial-structure optimization method for the coils of moving-coil magnetically levitated planar motors (MLPMs) to address the coupled challenges of power consumption and spatial constraints. The proposed framework systematically determines the optimal coil geometry and arrangement to minimize power consumption under a required force output and a strictly confined mover volume. A harmonic-based electromagnetic force model is employed to guide a compact coil layout by defining the number, length, and spacing of coils. These parameters are subsequently incorporated into a power-minimization model to determine the coil and beam widths. A final trade-off optimization is performed to balance high-order harmonic suppression and manufacturing tolerance, resulting in a comprehensive design strategy. Experimental results validate the superiority of the proposed method: under identical motor dimensions and magnetic pole pitch, the optimized design achieves more than a 40% increase in thrust-to-weight ratio (TWR) while reducing thrust fluctuation to below 15%. Furthermore, at a constant levitation height, the proposed design reduces power consumption by 10% to 25% compared with conventional systems. These findings demonstrate significant improvements in system stability and force efficiency, offering a generalized and practical design guideline for high-performance moving-coil MLPM.

title: A Direct Harmonic Current Suppression Technique for Dual Three-Phase PMSM System
abstract: Due to the small equivalent impedance in harmonic loop, the harmonic currents in dual three-phase permanent-magnet synchronous machine system are relatively large, which would lead to the serious distortion of phase currents and extra system loss. Hence, the suppression of harmonic currents is indispensable. To further improve the suppression performance, the simplified technique is proposed. In the proposed technique, two variable virtual voltage vectors, which are dynamically determined by the reference voltages, are designed and applied in modulation process, under both the fundamental-related sub-plane and the harmonic-related sub-planes. The novelty of the proposed technique is that the modulation implementation is greatly simplified while the harmonic currents are effectively suppressed, compared with the previous methods. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed technique is validated through the experimental test.

title: Analysis and Elimination of Current Measurement Scaling Error for High-Frequency Voltage Injection-Based Sensorless Control
abstract: Current measurement scaling error (CMSE) is a common problem in permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) drive systems. It can be categorized into current measurement scaling difference error (CMSDE) and current measurement scaling average error (CMSAE). This research aims to analyze and eliminate the effects of the CMSE on rotating high-frequency voltage injection (HFVI)-based sensorless control. Firstly, a detailed analysis of the CMSE-induced position estimation error is presented, revealing the relationship between the position estimation error and the CMSE. It indicates that the CMSE introduces both a DC offset and a 2nd harmonic into the position estimation. Secondly, an effective sequential elimination strategy is proposed to address the CMSDE as its first step, and then the CMSAE as the second step. A moving average filter (MAF) is designed to extract the error signal, followed by a sliding mode controller (SMC) to eliminate the CMSDE and CMSAE. Finally, the theoretical analysis and the elimination methods of the CMSE have been validated by the experimental results.

title: Fine-Grained Optimal Allocation of Wind Farm Decoupled Models for CPU-GPU Parallel EMT Simulation
abstract: Parallel. simulation based on CPU-GPU heterogeneous hardware, owing to its high speed-up ratio, has emerged as an effective approach for accelerating electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation of wind farms. However, most existing studies rely mainly on hardware multi-threading capabilities, with limited quantitative analysis of model–hardware adaptability, resulting in insufficient exploitation of the complementary advantages of CPUs and GPUs. To this end, this paper proposes a fine-grained optimal allocation method (FGOAM) that formulates the hardware assignment of each subsystem in wind farms as a constrained optimization problem for maximal simulation efficiency. Firstly, a bottom-up quantification method is developed to accurately assess the computational resources and solution time of decoupled models by decomposing the computation process into sequential and parallelizable steps. Secondly, a FGOAM for decoupled wind farm models is proposed, for the first time, by formulating an integer nonlinear programming (INLP) problem for step-level computation allocation. Finally, to further improve solution efficiency of FGOAM, an enhanced FGOAM (E-FGOAM) is derived via integer variable reduction without sacrificing allocation optimality. The accuracy of the proposed quantification method and the improvement on simulation efficiency after optimal allocation are validated. Simulation results demonstrate that the simulation speed is increased by two orders of magnitude for a wind farm consisting of 400 turbines.

title: Parallelizable Complex Neural Dynamics Models for PMSM Temperature Estimation With Hardware Acceleration
abstract: Accurate and efficient thermal dynamics models of permanent magnet synchronous motors are vital to efficient thermal management strategies. Physics-informed methods combine model-based and data-driven methods, offering greater flexibility than model-based methods and superior explainability compared to data-driven methods. Nonetheless, there are still challenges in balancing real-time performance, estimation accuracy, and explainability. This paper presents a hardware-efficient complex neural dynamics model achieved through the linear decoupling, diagonalization, and reparameterization of the state-space model, introducing a novel paradigm for the physics-informed method that offers high explainability and accuracy in electric motor temperature estimation tasks. We validate this physics-informed method on an NVIDIA A800 GPU using the JAX machine learning framework, the parallel prefix-sum algorithm, and the Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) platform. We demonstrate its superior estimation performance and parallelizable hardware acceleration capabilities through experimental evaluation on a real electric motor.

title: A dv / dt Output Filter for Mitigating Motor Terminal Overvoltage in SiC-Based Motor Drive Systems
abstract: The Silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFET, as a prominent wide bandgap device, is extensively used in motor drive systems due to its high-speed switching characteristic. However, higher dv/dt will cause overvoltage at the motor terminals, accelerate the aging of windings and bearings, seriously threaten the insulation of motor windings, and shorten the service life of the motor. To address the critical challenge, this paper proposes a novel third-order LCRL dv/dt filter topology, which introduces parallel inductance to improve the flexibility of cable matching and shunts damping resistors to reduce damping loss, thereby significantly reducing the volume and cost of the heat sink. A parameter design method suitable for high-order filters and a multi-dimensional design optimization strategy based on the optimal loss model are proposed to simultaneously find the best solution to minimize motor terminal overvoltage and total system loss, providing theoretical guidance for the application of high-order dv/dt filters. A series of experimental results demonstrate that the motor terminal overvoltage, damping loss, and volume of the proposed filter are reduced by 81.5%, 43.7%, and 33.3%, respectively, compared with the conventional LCR filter, which improves motor reliability in high-speed switching applications without compromising system efficiency.

title: Region-Driven Two-Layer Refined Scheduling for Multi-Stack-Integrated Alkaline Electrolyzer in Wind-Hydrogen System
abstract: To mitigate the stability impacts of renewable intermittency on power systems, on-site accommodation via Power-to-Hydrogen (P2H) stands out as a promising solution. As the most mature P2H technology, balance-of-plant (BOP)-shared multi-stack integrated alkaline water electrolyzer (MSI-AWE) systems offer both high flexibility and cost advantages. However, accommodating highly fluctuating wind power requires scheduling MSI-AWE system at minute-level intervals, posing significant computational burdens for real-time energy management. To address this, this paper first introduces the concept of operational regions to efficiently characterize the time-varying power boundaries of MSI-AWE systems, along with a pruning-based algorithm to accelerate region computation. Further, a minute-level model predictive control (MPC)-based wind-hydrogen operational framework is proposed, which decouples the refined scheduling problem into region-embedded upper-layer power allocation and lower-layer electrolyte/cooling flow regulation. Case studies demonstrate that the two-layer framework extends full wind power utilization duration by 8.7%, improves state regulation accuracy by 4.6%, and reduces average computation time by 50.2% compared to traditional single-layer approaches, validating its effectiveness in enhancing renewable energy accommodation and facilitating smart grid integration.

title: A Fully Distributed Market Clearing Framework for Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading in Heterogeneous Virtual Power Plants
abstract: Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) are proposed to aggregate numerous small-scale prosumers to handle their barriers in participating in Peer-to-Peer (P2P) markets due to capacity requirements. However, market clearing in P2P energy markets with multiple VPPs is challenging because of VPP heterogeneity, communication resource constraints, and the coupling between intra- and inter-VPP markets. This paper constructs a market clearing framework for this scenery. The fully distributed P2P energy market is designed for inter-VPP market with high communication costs and the intra-VPP market with insufficient communication resources to release the communication burden, while other intra-VPP market apply the distributed framework. Under such a setting, through the reconstruction of the fully - distributed P2P energy market clearing problem based on distributed estimation, the P2P energy market clearing problem for multiple heterogeneous virtual power plants is constructed. A market clearing algorithm is developed based on the consensus ADMM and parallel ADMM to maximize the utilization of communication resources and improving communication efficiency. Furthermore, based on marginal cost pricing, the electricity prices in the heterogeneous intra-VPP markets and inter-VPP market are discussed. Finally, the convergence and scalability of the proposed algorithm and the effectiveness of the electricity price analysis are verified on the IEEE 37-bus and IEEE 123-bus test feeders.

title: Droop-Based Hierarchical Control for Power-Sharing and Voltage Balancing in Bipolar DC Microgrids
abstract: Bipolar DC microgrids, which consist of three lines and three voltage buses, are increasingly being explored in modern power systems as they can provide higher reliability and flexibility compared to unipolar systems. One of the main assignments of bipolar DC microgrids is the efficient operation through power-sharing between converters. However, compared to unipolar systems, there are more considerations to operate bipolar systems such as power coupling across three buses, unbalanced load, and voltage imbalance. To settle the above considerations, this article presents droop-based hierarchical control in bipolar DC microgrid, consisting of primary and secondary control levels. The primary level performs power-sharing through droop control, which is designed based on the equivalent droop circuit model of bipolar DC microgrid and analysis of power coupling and load imbalance conditions. The second level is implemented through low-bandwidth communication and performs voltage restoration and balancing bipolar bus voltages or SoC of energy storage systems in the bipolar DC microgrid. Stability analysis of the entire control system including primary and second control levels is conducted. Finally, the operation and effectiveness of the proposed hierarchical control are validated via lab-scale DC microgrid experiments.

title: PLL-Free Approach: Reactive Power-Based Synchronization in Grid-Following Inverters
abstract: The rapid growth in inverter-based resource penetration is leading to the widespread integration of grid-following and grid-forming inverters within ac grids. Despite their distinct operational characteristics, these two inverter modes share fundamental similarities, motivating joint investigations into their attributes. Building on the identified symmetry between these devices, this paper proposes a novel phase-locked loop-free grid-following control strategy inspired by the grid-forming control architecture. The proposed approach simplifies the grid-following inverter control structure while retaining its inherent capabilities and enabling the intuitive configuration of synchronous inertia and damping. Analytical, experimental, and simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

title: A Cross-Line Successive Fault Detection of Distribution Network Based on Zero-Sequence Capacitance Variation
abstract: In non-effectively grounded system, the rise in phase voltage during single-phase grounding (SPG) fault poses a significant threat to the system’s insulation integrity. The increasing cabling rate in distribution network has led to a rising proportion of cross-line double successive single-phase grounding (SSPG) faults triggered by initial fault. To address the challenges of weak characteristic and difficult detection of such successive fault, this paper proposes a SSPG detection method based on zero-sequence capacitance variation. First, the dynamic zero-sequence equivalent network during successive faults is simplified, and derive the zero-sequence current (ZSC) expressions for each feeder under both overdamped and underdamped conditions. Subsequently, the singular value decomposition-total least squares extended Prony algorithm is employed to fit the zero-sequence voltage (ZSV) and ZSC, enabling the calculation of zero-sequence capacitance for both initial and successive faults in the complex frequency domain. A detection criterion is then constructed using the variation of capacitance. Finally, digital simulations and recorded field data validate the correctness and feasibility of the theoretical analysis.

title: Situationally Aware Rolling Horizon Multi-Tier Load Restoration Considering Behind-the-Meter DER
abstract: Restoration in power distribution systems (PDSs) is well studied, however, most existing research focuses on network partition and microgrid formation, where load transfer is limited to adjacent feeders. This focus is not practical, as when adjacent feeders lack sufficient capacity, utilities may request support from more distant feeders in practice. Such a hierarchical restoration is complex, especially when involving changing system conditions due to cold load pickup and delayed reconnection of behind-the-meter DERs. To fill this research gap, a situationally aware multi-tier load restoration framework is proposed. Specifically, models are proposed to describe the multi-tier load restoration, including the multi-tier load transfer and substation transformer and feeder protection models. By introducing binary actional switching variables and load block transfer variables, the models effectively captures the dynamics of switches and multi-tier transfer process. To integrate situational awareness of evolving system conditions, the problem is formulated as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) and then embedded within a rolling horizon optimization. Particularly, a set of safeguarded constraints are developed based on segment-level restoration reward bounds to mitigate the myopia of traditional rolling horizon optimization. The proposed safeguarded rolling strategy guarantees that each time step is lower bounded by a $(1-\varepsilon)$ -fraction of its optimal restoration potential, thereby balancing short-term switching decisions with long-term restoration goals. Finally, cases studies on the modified IEEE 123-node test feeder validate the proposed multi-tier restoration framework.

title: Static Voltage Stability and DGs Integration Capacity Quantification Method With Extended Power Flow for ADNs With Grid-Forming and Grid-Following DGs
abstract: Power flow calculation and static voltage stability (SVS) analysis of active distribution networks (ADNs) are facing convergence and applicability issues caused by extreme conditions and control strategies of grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) distributed generations (DGs). To solve these challenges, an SVS and DG integration capacity quantification method based on extended holomorphic embedding power flow (EHEPF) is proposed which includes four aspects: 1) an EHEPF algorithm is developed that accommodates both convergence and converter’s internal primary and secondary control characteristics of DGs; 2) the unsolvable mathematical expression of EHEPF is derived using Padé approximant to clearly distinguish between no solution and lower-branch (inoperable) solution; 3) the voltage sensitivity and SVS indexes of EHEPF combining different control strategies of DGs are formulated to analyze the weak bus and SVS of ADNs; 4) the DGs integration capacity is quantified by balancing SVS and network loss under voltage distribution calculated in EHEPF. Case studies are carried out on 12 bus, IEEE 33 and IEEE 123 bus systems. Numerous test results are analyzed to verify the applicability, convergence and effectiveness of proposed EHEPF for SVS and DGs integration capacity quantification in ADNs.

title: An End-to-End Learning Model With Quantization Technology for Dynamic Prediction-Decision Joint-Making in Active Distribution Networks
abstract: Efficient load management and system stability in active distribution networks (ADNs) depend heavily on accurate forecasting of photovoltaic (PV) generation, load demand, and reliable dynamic decision-making. This paper proposes a novel end-to-end joint learning model for dynamic prediction-decision joint-making in active distribution networks. The model integrates a prediction module, leveraging attentional-quantization long short-term memory (AQLSTM) networks to forecast photovoltaic generation, active power load, and reactive power load, with a control decision module based on Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3). The forecasting outputs are fed into the decision-making module, enabling dynamic adjustments to network parameters. A feedback mechanism is introduced which incorporates decision losses into the prediction module to enhance forecasting accuracy, thereby creating a tightly coupled, end-to-end joint optimization framework. In addition, a sensitivity-aware mixed-precision quantization technology is adopted to reduce computational overhead and facilitate efficient deployment. Experimental results on IEEE 33-bus and 123-bus distribution networks demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms other methods in terms of forecasting accuracy and dynamic control effectiveness, resulting in substantial improvements in the operational efficiency and stability of ADNs.

title: Low Carbon Scheduling of Integrated Energy System Based on Large Language Model-Embedded Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The complex multi-energy coupling characteristics inherent to integrated energy system (IES) present unprecedented challenges for the implementation of low-carbon scheduling. Existing optimization methods often exhibit limitations in system scalability, algorithm adaptivity, and carbon reduction efficacy for complex IES. This paper proposes a Large Language Model (LLM)-Embedded Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (LEMARL) to address the aforementioned issues. The proposed method integrates the global perception capability of LLMs with the dynamic optimization capability of MARL. Specifically, the LLM-Embedded module generates high-quality reward functions and policy frameworks from a global perspective, while the MARL module leverages these LLM-generated strategies for distributed interactive iterations—greatly enhancing computation efficiency and scalability. Simulation results demonstrate that LEMARL reduces carbon emissions by 7.76% and simultaneously decreases operating costs by 4.49% in a small-scale IES. Furthermore, LEMARL also exhibits superior applicability and scalability in large-scale IES of the IEEE 141-bus power grid integrated with 51-node thermal system.

title: Probabilistic Disaggregation of Behind-the-Meter PV Systems Using Conformal Prediction
abstract: Disaggregating solar photovoltaics (PV) profiles from smart electricity meter data has attracted attention, as Distribution System Operators (DSOs) need street-level PV generation profiles to improve grid operations and planning. Given the importance of reliability in operational decisions, probabilistic results are preferred to avoid overlooking potential violations. This paper proposes a probabilistic disaggregation framework based on Conformal Prediction (CP), a cutting-edge uncertainty quantification methodology. This framework trains a deterministic regressor to estimate normalized PV generation profiles and proposes an efficient capacity estimation algorithm to help compute the full PV generation profiles. To obtain probabilistic results, the framework applied CP with different variants, such as Mondrian Binning (MB) and Conformal Predictive System (CPS), to enhance the reliability of prediction intervals. To address the arbitrary bin count in CP with MB, the paper proposes a novel CP variant, namely: Adaptive Mondrian Binning (AMB). Its performance, along with other CP methods, is evaluated and benchmarked against quantile regression methods on two actual datasets from the region of Amsterdam, the Netherlands, and Sydney, Australia. Results show that using LightGBM as the deterministic regressor, AMB outperforms quantile regression and other CP variants. The generalizability of the proposed framework is analysed for both probabilistic outputs and key sub-processes, such as deterministic disaggregation and capacity estimation.

title: Multi-Time Scale Distributed Stochastic Economic Dispatch for Flexible Traction Power Supply System
abstract: Flexible traction power supply system (FTPSS), integrated with renewable energy, energy storage, and power flow controllers (PFC), offers great potential for safe and economical railway operation. However, the uncertainty in traction load and photovoltaic (PV) output poses significant challenges to cost-effective dispatch. Therefore, a multi-time scale distributed stochastic economic dispatch method for FTPSS is proposed. The prediction module uses LSTM to produce point forecasts, while KDE models the forecast errors to construct predictive intervals and generate scenarios for PV output and traction load. A stochastic programming model is then formulated, where uncertainties in traction load and PV are represented by chance constraints and scenarios. In the first stage, the day-ahead forecast is used to solve the stochastic optimization model to minimize daily operational cost. In the second stage, the scheduler uses the day-ahead plan as a soft reference and re-optimizes at each rolling step with updated probabilistic forecasts, implementing only the first control move to maintain real-time responsiveness and economic efficiency. The optimization model is solved using an ADMM-based distributed algorithm, which accounts for limited inter-subsystem communication and reduces computational complexity. A case study based on a real electrified railway demonstrates that the proposed method improves economic performance by reducing operating costs by approximately 9% under uncertainty.

title: Dynamic Behavior Modeling of Price-Responsive Flexible Loads: A Deep Learning-Parameterized Inverse Optimization Approach
abstract: Accurately modeling the behavior of price-responsive flexible loads (PRFLs) is increasingly critical for enhancing power system flexibility. While existing inverse optimization methods can achieve flexible load modeling using only external price-response data, the surrogate model with time-invariant parameters severely limits its ability to capture dynamic behaviors induced by user demands, weather conditions, etc. In contrast to mainstream static modeling formulations, this paper proposes a Deep Learning-parameterized Inverse Optimization (DL-IO) method that enables dynamic surrogate modeling of PRFLs. Specifically, a dynamic virtual energy storage (DVES) model is formulated as the surrogate model, with its parameters represented by multi-task deep learning to exhibit time-varying properties. Then, the DVES model is integrated into the DL-IO framework, enabling the approximation of response behaviors for thermostatically controlled loads (TCLs) and electric vehicles (EVs) based solely on price-response data and public information. To solve the resulting bi-level DL-IO problem, it is reformulated as an empirical risk minimization task, which consists of a deep learning-based parameter estimation layer and an optimization-based response estimation layer. An analytical end-to-end gradient is then derived and backpropagated through both layers to achieve behavior learning. Numerical tests indicate that the proposed modeling method outperforms existing inverse optimization and data-driven regression approaches.

title: Andronov-Hopf Oscillator-Based Harmonic Elimination Scheme for Grid-Connected Inverters
abstract: Conventional harmonic elimination methods for Grid-Connected Inverters (GCI) rely on individual harmonic extraction and compensation, resulting in increased complexity and slow dynamic response. In this paper, the Virtual Oscillator based Harmonic Compensation (VO-HC) is proposed. It uses the Andronov–Hopf oscillator not for synchronization or grid-forming purposes, but to extract the fundamental component from the distorted grid current. The Hopf oscillator is inherently frequency-adaptive, allowing it to extract the fundamental component and attenuate harmonics with negligible phase delay compared to traditional filters. The extractor provides unity-gain fundamental tracking even under frequency deviations and weak-grid conditions. The extracted fundamental is then subtracted from the measured grid current to isolate the grid current harmonics. These harmonics are compensated using a simple proportional compensator loop in the stationary frame as a feedforward, operating in parallel with a conventional Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) current controller. This results in fast low-order harmonic compensation of grid current, improving the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of the GCI system. Experimental results demonstrate THD reduction from up to 18.4% to below 2.5%, with a transient settling time of approximately 2–3 ms. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through both simulation and experimental results conducted on a laboratory two-inverter microgrid setup under distorted and weak-grid conditions.

title: Centralized Multi-Functional Power Management of an Integrated Microgrid–Electric Vehicle Charging Station
abstract: Various power management systems for microgrids (MGs) integrated with electric vehicle (EV) charging stations (CSs) have been designed so far, each addressing different aspects of grid-connected or off-grid operation. However, no previous research has developed multi-objective power management schemes that encompass all possible operating modes, including MG operation with the grid (G) without CS, CS operation with G without MG, MG-CS integrated operation with G, MG and CS autonomous operation in off-grid mode, and the interaction between MG and CS without G. In this article, innovative multi-functional power management strategies utilizing centralized control system have been modeled and designed for the aforementioned operational modes and simulated in the time-domain nonlinear environment of the MATLAB-SIMULINK. The results indicate the effective performance of different schemes in various operational states.

title: Simplicial Graph-Based Detection and Localization of Cyber Attacks Against Large-Scale Smart Grids
abstract: Ensuring the resilience of large-scale power systems against cyber attacks is critical to maintaining the stability of modern cyber-physical energy systems. Existing machine learning (ML)-based detection frameworks predominantly focus on pairwise node interactions (i.e., edges) and often overlook capturing higher-order topological structures (i.e., simplicial complexes) that emerge within power networks. This paper introduces a novel simplicial recurrent graph neural network (SRGNN) for attack detection and localization in large-scale smart grid infrastructure. Unlike conventional graph models, SRGNN incorporates higher-order simplicial interactions to capture group-wise dependencies among buses and transmission lines, allowing the model to better reflect the multi-scale dynamics of grid operation and control. We investigate the robustness of our model against benchmark and proposed complex simplicial-based attack node selection strategies. Our extensive experiments on large-scale transmission power networks (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$2{,}869$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-bus, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$9{,}241$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-bus, and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$70{,}000$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-bus systems) demonstrate that the proposed SRGNN model outperforms ML-based benchmark models, achieving superior detection and localization performance by 9–39% and 8–35%, respectively, in detection rate against complex attacks. These results underscore the importance of modeling higher-order topological structures for robust and scalable security in power systems.

title: Nanometric layered coating assembly bridging across micro-electronics and mega-voltage power grids
abstract: Electrical insulation remains a universal and critical challenge across electronic and electrical systems, from micro-electronics to mega-volt power grids. Many insulation failures originate from adverse interfacial processes, including carrier injection, surface flashover, and discharge erosion. This article highlights a scalable, technologically viable, and unified surface engineering solution based on conformal, self-assembled 2D nanocoating, which provide multifunctional barrier protection under extreme electrical, environmental, and thermal stresses. We envision this self-assembled nanocoating as a holistic dielectric surface re-engineering approach, enabling the next generation of electrification technologies.

title: Demand Response Potential Evaluation for Commercial HVAC Loads Considering Cooling Storage in Chilled Water Loops
abstract: Commercial HVAC systems offer great potential for demand response (DR). Existing methods for HVAC DR evaluation often neglect the cooling storage effect within chilled water loops. However, this effect provides substantial flexibility and its omission leads to considerable underestimation of DR potential. Incorporating this effect poses major modeling and computational challenges due to the spatiotemporal variation of chilled water temperature and the complex coupled dynamics between chilled water loops and the indoor environment. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel method for evaluating HVAC DR potential considering cooling storage. First, we develop a model for chilled water loops based on 1-D advection-diffusion partial differential equations (PDEs). Then, a stepwise solution approach that leverages the identified stepwise rising pattern in chilled water temperature during DR events is proposed to solve the physical process effectively without directly solving the full PDEs. A high-fidelity simulation platform is established to validate the proposed method. Results indicate that, in most scenarios, the DR potential evaluated with the cooling storage effect is more than twice as high as that evaluated without it.

title: High-performance and fast-regenerative passive body cooling enabled by a highly ordered polyacrylamide hydrogel
abstract: Efficient, regenerative, and low-cost cooling materials are highly desirable for personal thermal management under heat stress, yet existing cooling patches often suffer from limited cooling performance or poor reusability. Here, a theoretically guided hydrogel cooling patch with vertically aligned, low-tortuosity pores enables efficient passive evaporative cooling and instant regeneration. This work offers a sustainable, cost-effective strategy for personal thermal management and may inspire next-generation fast-regenerative passive cooling devices.

title: Temporal and spatial separations between spin glass and short-range order
abstract: Broken-symmetry-induced order parameters account for many phenomena in condensed matter physics. For spin glasses, such a framework dictates its theoretical construction, whereas experiments have only established dynamical behaviors such as frequency dependent magnetic susceptibility and aging but not the thermodynamic phase. Experimental techniques have limitations when the spin glass is probed as an isolated state. To resolve this conundrum, we create an evolution from long-range order using a well-controlled tuning of the disorder on a spinel's sublattice. Cross-referencing a series of specimens at both long (milliseconds to seconds) and short (picosecond) time scales illustrates the relationship between spin glass and long- and short-range orders. The dynamics of short- and long-range order formations are not affected by disorder, as revealed by neutron magnetic diffuse scattering, however the ranges of these orderings are changed by the introduced disorder. Across all specimens, the inflection point of the correlation length's temperature dependence fully matches with the peak in heat capacity, while spin glass can freeze either below or well above this characteristic temperature of spin order formation. Our results identify an uncorrelated coexistence of the two and attribute components of the spin glass to individual spins at domain walls between spin clusters.

title: Piezoelectric response in ionic liquids and electrolytes through dynamic phase transitions
abstract: Piezoelectricity, the generation of electric charge under mechanical stress or effecting strain under an applied electric field, has powered technologies from quartz oscillators to modern actuators. The direct piezoelectric effect, traditionally confined to solid-state materials, has recently been demonstrated in room-temperature ionic liquids (RTILs) and deep eutectic solvents (DESs). This perspective showcases recent experimental outcomes, mechanistic insights, and structural dependencies to outline a roadmap for exploiting liquid-phase piezo-electrics. Highlighting the role of pressure-induced liquid-to-crystalline transitions, ion pair organization, and compositional tuning, we propose design strategies that could unlock applications ranging from flexible sensors to piezo-pneumatic devices. Unlike traditional liquids, where the application of pressure transfers mechanical load with no chemical or physical change, in these systems, the applied stress triggers a physical or chemical transformation, such as a phase transition, crystallization, or a change in molecular ordering. Such transformations are particularly important because they can generate non-centrosymmetric crystalline domains, which are essential for the emergence of piezoelectric behavior. This phenomenon is especially relevant in solid polymer electrolytes, where stress-induced crystallization can impart piezoelectric functionality. These materials are of particular interest for energy-harvesting composites, in which the multifunctional interfaces between piezoelectric phases and conductive matrices play a critical role in determining overall electromechanical performance.

title: Breaking the power ceiling of radiative cooling through evaporative-radiative synergy
abstract: Radiative cooling is a pivotal technology for sustainable thermal management, yet its broad adoption is constrained by a fundamental power ceiling (∼150 W m−2) and strong dependence on atmospheric conditions. This review highlights evaporative-assisted radiative cooling as an emerging strategy that effectively bypasses this constraint. The combined mechanism enables hybrid systems to achieve unprecedented, climate-resilient cooling power. We analyze the thermodynamic principles underlying this synergy, where radiative cooling elevates evaporative performance beyond its standalone limit, and evaporation, in turn, enhances the net cooling flux. We then critically review the material embodiments of this concept, from decoupled tandem and monolithic porous structures to adaptive systems. Their application potential spans from building envelopes and personal thermal management to electronics cooling and agriculture. Finally, we discuss the critical challenges of durability, dynamic climate adaptation, and system integration that must be surmounted for practical deployment. By establishing a unified framework and scalable design principles, this work outlines a pathway toward next-generation high-performance passive cooling technologies essential for global energy sustainability.

title: Self-powered magnetoelastic tents for sustainable energy access in unhoused communities
abstract: Access to reliable, clean energy remains a major challenge for the unhoused and off-grid communities. Here, we introduce a self-powered magnetoelastic tent that leverages the giant magnetoelastic effect to harvest energy from human motion and environmental stimuli. The smart tent integrates magnetoelastic textiles, consisting of a magnetomechanical coupling layer and a magnetic induction layer, converting mechanical motion into electricity. Optimizing weaving patterns, layer stacking, and conductive fiber turns enables robust energy generation, with a representative magnetoelastic textile unit delivering a maximum instantaneous power of 0.094 mW, stable operation over 12,000 continuous cycles, and intrinsic waterproof performance. Simple hand tapping can charge a 0.22-μF capacitor to 5.80 V within 1.5 s, providing sufficient power for small electronics. Lightweight, recyclable, and weather resistant, the tents maintain stable performance under representative outdoor conditions. This work presents a scalable platform for sustainable, decentralized energy harvesting to expand supplementary energy access in temporary shelter settings.

title: Optimizing P2P Energy Trading Using Internet of Things and Agentic AI Cluster Zooming
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become the game changer in smart grids-an enabler of network autonomy, self-healing, and reconfiguration. This study integrates AI and Internet of Things (IoT) to organise peer-to-peer (P2P) energy prosumers into virtual clusters without altering the physical topology of the power network. The aim is to enable an autonomous, scalable and dynamic virtual microgrids (VMG) by leveraging federated learning, agentic AI, AI agents, IoT, and cluster zooming to optimise P2P energy trading costs for prosumers and operational expenditure (OPEX) for network operators, depending on the number of prosumers available. The study employs a central controller AI to coordinate multiple local AI agents. Each AI agent resides in the network server and monitors energy trading traffic for each long-range wide-area network (LoRaWAN) gateway to optimise trading and OPEX costs via cluster zooming achieved by the spreading factor (SF) via adaptive data rate (ADR) mechanism of LoRaWAN. The agentic AI module in the cloud autonomously selects and adapts the network coverage based on SF, via the AI energy trading agent configured in the LoRaWAN access network server, to zoom the clusters (i.e., VMGs) in grid-connected and island modes. The study formulates an energy trading model connecting the physical (electrical) and virtual (telecom) distances and OPEX in the VMG. With agentic AI-assisted cluster zooming, over 70% of the energy is traded at lower SF. At the same time, the energy costs decrease by 40% in proportion to the network size and the number of prosumers. For the network operator, OPEX reduces by 21% and 38% in base-station power consumption. Ultimately, grid-connected prosumers pay higher charges than their off-grid counterparts. The agentic AI model in this study exemplifies a use case of the 3GPP model of the future 6G network.

title: Phase Shift Groups in Power Flow Analysis for Improved Power Systems Modeling
abstract: This letter presents an algorithm that efficiently and consistently represents, in the positive-sequence power flow, the phase shifts introduced by wye–delta-connected transformers. As is well known, wye–delta transformers impose fixed voltage and current phase shifts in multiples of 30 degrees. Because these shifts do not affect bus voltage magnitudes or branch power flows, they are frequently omitted or modeled inconsistently. However, non-uniform representation of transformer phase shifts can introduce artificial voltage-angle discontinuities that negatively impact Newton-based power flow convergence. To address this issue, the letter introduces the concept of Phase Shift Groups (PSGs), which enforce consistent voltage-angle representation across the power system model. The proposed PSG-aware initialization yields a physically consistent starting point that improves Newton-Raphson convergence robustness compared to conventional flat-start methods. Beyond initialization, PSGs provide a systematic mechanism for data-quality validation, flagging incomplete or inconsistent transformer connection data. Scalability is demonstrated on systems with up to 110,000 buses with negligible computational overhead.

title: Ferroelectricity in six-ångström-thick two-dimensional gallium oxide
abstract: When β-Ga2O3 is thinned to the half-unit-cell limit, it can undergo a strain-induced phase transition that leads to intrinsic ferroelectricity with a polarization switching voltage of 0.8 V, meeting the voltage-scaling requirements of complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology.

title: Aggregating DER Uncertainty: Minkowski Sum Under Joint Chance Constraints
abstract: Addressing uncertainty is essential in power systems with high levels of renewable energy penetration. Distributed energy resources (DERs), due to their partially controllable nature, are a major source of uncertainty. However, due to their large numbers and complex correlations, their aggregated uncertainty is highly complex. This paper aims to track how the uncertainty is modeled from individual DER prediction errors to the aggregated-level. By enforcing a specified confidence level, the aggregated-level probabilistic flexibility boundary is formulated as a Minkowski sum under joint chance constraints (JCCs). Despite the inherent intractability of this problem, we establish an equivalent representation that allows for an effective approximation using the proposed quantile cube approximation method. An iterative algorithm is also developed to enhance computational efficiency in implementing the method. Numerical tests demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces the conservativeness of the aggregated confidence boundary and the computation time at the same time.

title: Time-Efficient and Tractable DRCC-Based Optimal Operation of EV Charging Stations Under Uncertainty
abstract: With the growing penetration of electric vehicles (EVs), efficient and robust operation of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) has become increasingly important. This article proposes an optimal scheduling problem for multiple EVCSs, while considering uncertainties in individual EVs’ forecasted arrival/departure times and desired energy demands. To address this, a distributionally robust chance-constraint (DRCC)-based optimization framework is proposed, which utilizes a Wasserstein distance-based ambiguity set. Considering the above EV uncer-tainty parameters, a general DRCC formulation for EVCS-level constraints is difficult to achieve. The proposed optimization framework maps the above EV uncertainty parameters into a single uncertainty parameter of EVCS total charging power, thereby enabling a general DRCC formulation. In addition, EV constraints are formulated to allow arrival/departure times to be treated as continuous rather than discrete time intervals. We also propose a time efficient DRCC reformulation method that considers the physical limits of the uncertainty parameter. Case studies based on real-world EVCS data are conducted to validate the operational efficiency and robustness of the proposed method for multiple EVCSs.

title: Electrostatic-electromagnetic coupling regulates wireless energy interaction for interference shielding
abstract: Electronic systems are facing challenges of adaptive electromagnetic compatibility in dynamic environments. The authors demonstrate a TENG-enabled EMI shielding system that interacts with wireless electromagnetic energy by electrostatic-electromagnetic coupling. The triboelectrically generated built-in electric fields within PDMS@MXene/PPy@CF reshape the charge confinement and polarization dynamics under electromagnetic irradiation, optimizing the EMI shielding performance. This work advances electromagnetic compatibility design from passive protection to active energy management.

title: The rise of renewable energy: How it shapes dependency, diversity, and geopolitical risk in the European Union
abstract: As the European Union advances its shift toward cleaner energy to address climate challenges, a pressing question emerges: can this shift also strengthen energy security in an increasingly volatile global landscape? This study investigates the impact of renewable energy on energy security risks across 27 EU countries over the period 2010 to 2022. It measures energy security through three key dimensions—energy dependency risk, energy diversity risk, and geopolitical risk. The findings reveal that renewable energy significantly mitigates energy diversity risk and geopolitical risk across the EU. However, its impact on energy dependency risk is statistically insignificant in the overall sample. Notably, further non-linear analyses show that in countries with higher levels of renewable energy deployment, renewables significantly reduce dependency risk on foreign energy sources. This highlights the importance of reaching a critical threshold of renewable integration to unlock broader energy security benefits.

title: Hierarchical Distributed Control With Projected Gradient Descent for Real-Time Congestion Mitigation in MVDC Distribution Systems
abstract: Ineffective congestion management in medium-voltage DC distribution system risks thermal overloads, voltage violations, and systemic instability. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a distributed congestion mitigation method via adaptive real-time control. First, a hierarchical control framework integrating congestion constraints is established, with optimality conditions rigorously derived. Second, the upper layer generates dispatch references to guide lower-layer operations. Projection operators are then introduced to reformulate optimality conditions for controller compatibility, enabling distributed optimal control laws based on projected gradient descent. This approach achieves real-time congestion management and optimal operation. Simulations and comparisons are conducted on a modified IEEE 33 medium-voltage DC distribution system. Compared to model predictive control, the proposed method achieves reduced fluctuations under varying operating conditions. In contrast to distributed robust optimization, it exhibits superior economic performance.

title: Decomposition and Stacked Meta-Learning for Short-Term Electric Vehicle Load Forecasting
abstract: Accurate short-term electric vehicle (EV) load forecasting is critical for grid stability and demand response management amid rapidly increasing EV penetration. However, existing statistical, ensemble, and deep learning models often rely on implicit sequence learning and struggle to jointly capture multi-scale temporal structure, nonlinear interactions, and cross-dataset heterogeneity in EV charging demand. This paper proposes a decomposition-driven hybrid forecasting framework that integrates Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess (STL) with component-specific learning and stacked ensemble fusion. The EV load signal is decomposed into trend, seasonal, and residual components, each modeled using an algorithm aligned with its statistical characteristics. Component-level predictions are then fused through a Gradient Boosting Regressor meta-learner to enhance robustness and generalization. Experimental evaluation on four real-world EV charging datasets (ACN, Palo Alto, Perth, and Paris) demonstrates consistent performance gains over representative statistical, ensemble, and deep learning baselines. On the ACN dataset, the proposed framework achieves MAE 0.614, RMSE 0.797, and MAPE 12.7%, corresponding to more than 90% and 88% reductions in RMSE and MAPE, respectively, relative to the strongest benchmark. These results highlight the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach for practical smart grid deployment.

title: A Two-Stage Profit Allocation Method for Virtual Power Plants Based on the Propensity to Disrupt
abstract: This article proposes a two-stage profit allocation method for virtual power plants (VPPs) to aggregate distributed energy resources (DERs) to participate in the electricity market. Based on the cooperative game theory, the proposed method allocates the profit by equalizing all DERs’ Propensity to Disrupt (DP) values, which are indices representing willingness to cooperate. The proposed approach is proven to be sustainable and defines an optimal solution to the Nash Bargaining problem. Considering uncertainties, the profit is initially assigned based on the ex-ante DP values determined in the day-ahead stage and then adjusted based on DERs’ actual contributions to the VPP in the real-time stage, forming a corrected two-stage process that mitigates excessive penalties or rewards found in ex-post-only and traditional two-stage allocation. In addition, the VPP operator’s (VPPO) profit is further allocated through modeling the operator as a member of the cooperative game. Numerical simulations confirm the balance and sustainability of the proposed allocation method.

title: Optimal Planning of Voltage-Regulating Active Power Filters for Meshed Cable Distribution Networks Considering Harmonic Propagation Paths
abstract: With the widespread application of cable lines in urban distribution grids, the amplification of harmonic standing waves has become increasingly prominent, leading to significant power quality deterioration. To mitigate this issue, this paper proposes an optimal planning strategy for voltage-regulating active power filters (VRAPFs) in meshed cable distribution grids, explicitly accounting for harmonic propagation paths. First, a harmonic propagation model is established to characterize typical scenarios with varying propagation characteristics. Subsequently, K-means clustering is applied to the propagation coefficients, partitioning the distribution grid into regions where nodes exhibit similar harmonic behaviors. Within each region, the node with the highest propagation coefficient is selected as the installation site of the VRAPF to ensure uniform harmonic suppression. Furthermore, the operational parameters of the VRAPF are optimized to simultaneously satisfy network performance requirements and minimize total cost. Comparative analyses with alternative site-selection strategies validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed approach.

title: Optimal Harmonic Control Strategy for Distribution Networks Considering the Actual Operating Characteristics of Voltage-Regulating Active Power Filter
abstract: An integrated harmonic optimization strategy for distribution networks typically models control devices as ideal current sources, formulating a convex optimization problem with multiple constraints. However, due to inherent nonlinearities, these devices often exhibit frequency coupling effects, leading to non-ideal harmonic control behavior. This article proposes a harmonic optimal control strategy for distribution networks that accounts for the actual operating characteristics of voltage-regulating active power filters (VRAPFs). First, a complete harmonic state-space (HSS) model of the VRAPF is developed to quantitatively analyze the internal signal exchange process between internal modules of VRAPF, thereby elucidating the mechanism behind frequency coupling effects. Second, a coupled virtual admittance model of the VRAPF is established to reshape the network impedance for improved harmonic suppression. Third, a multi-timescale harmonic control strategy based on coordinated global-local operation is proposed, enabling effective mitigation of harmonic injection uncertainties and ensuring that the harmonic voltage distortion at all distribution-network nodes remains below 4%. The proposed approach is validated through hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness and practicality.

title: Tractable Attack Detection With Robustness Certificate for Nonlinear Power Systems Under Stochastic Disturbances
abstract: This article presents a tractable attack detection methodology for nonlinear power systems that reduces complexity while providing a formal certificate of robustness against stochastic power disturbances. The inherent nonlinearity of power system dynamics typically necessitates sophisticated detection algorithms, while stochastic disturbances (e.g., fluctuating renewables) may introduce unforeseen behaviors that obscure attack discernment. This leads to two primary challenges: (i) model-based methods offer strong analytical foundations but may suffer from high computational complexity and rely on prior assumptions about disturbance distributions (e.g., Gaussianity); (ii) data-driven methods address uncertainty using statistical properties of large datasets or empirical validation within neural network architectures, yet they may lack performance guarantees. To this end, we propose (i) a linear detector that encodes stochastic disturbances through quadratic constraints, transforming the robust design problem into a convex quadratic program (QP), thereby ensuring tractability, and (ii) a robustness certificate that provides probabilistic guarantees in unseen scenarios with a desired confidence, based on the behavior of the optimal solution in active constraints (i.e., constraints that are equalities at the optimum). Unlike existing methods, our detection approach leverages the optimality properties of convex optimization to deliver performance guarantees without depending on prior assumptions or large datasets. We validate our method on cyber attack detection in Automatic Generation Control (AGC) within a two-area IEEE 118-bus system.

title: A Reinforcement Learning-Adapter Renewable Energy Forecasting Framework for Two-Stage Distribution Network Scheduling
abstract: With deepening renewable penetration, distribution-network operators must rely on high-quality forecasts to schedule distributed energy resources. However, most existing Prediction–then–Optimization (PTO) approaches rely solely on forecasted values as inputs, while overlooking the significant impact of the coupling between actual and forecasted values on operational costs. This limitation hinders the practicality and deployment of many decision-oriented methods in power systems. To address this issue, this paper investigates the two-stage scheduling problem of distribution networks and formulates it as a Coupled Prediction–then–Optimization (CPTO) problem. Then, we propose a RL-driven decision-focused framework that integrates a Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT)-based forecasting module with an improved Actor–Critic Reinforcement Learning (RL) adapter. Specifically, a GPT-based forecasting model with task-adaptive loss is proposed to capture the temporal characteristics of renewable energy outputs. On this basis, an RL adapter is designed to learn a decision-focused policy that dynamically refines the base forecasts, thereby effectively reducing the actual operating cost of the distribution network. Case studies on the IEEE 33-bus, IEEE 141-bus and IEEE 570-bus systems demonstrate that, compared with best baselines, the proposed framework reduces operational costs by 2.20%, 2.28% and 1.80% respectively, thereby validating its effectiveness and superiority in terms of both economic efficiency and operational reliability.

title: Winding Process Simulation and Stress Analysis of Rotor Retained by Carbon Fiber Sleeve for High-Speed Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: Rotor stress analysis of high-speed permanent magnet machines (HSPMMs) is a crucial step in the early design stage, directly affecting the reliability and service life of the HSPMM. To accurately analyze the stress of the rotor retained by carbon fiber sleeve that is assembled by tension winding, this paper proposes an equivalent deformation method (EDM), aiming to simulate the process of winding the rotor with carbon fiber tow. Firstly, the stress model of rotor retained by multi-layer carbon fiber sleeve is analyzed. The EDM is proposed based on actual winding process. Then, taking a 300 kW, 50,000 r/min HSPMM as an example, the winding process is simulated. The results obtained by the proposed method are consistent with those of the existing methods. Further, the stresses of the rotor at four states after winding are analyzed. Finally, the static rotor contact pressure measurement and rotor overspeed test indicate the validity of the proposed method.

title: Coordinated Load Frequency Control for Multi-Frequency Oscillations in Wind-Pumped Storage Hybrid Microgrids
abstract: Hybrid microgrids (MGs), particularly those incorporating wind power and pumped storage, have been widely adopted for renewable energy generation. However, hydraulic characteristics of pumped storage units (PSUs) and inter-generator interactions induce inevitably multi-frequency oscillations during load frequency control (LFC). To capture these oscillation behaviors and achieve effective suppression, this paper proposes a coordinated LFC strategy for hybrid MGs that integrates high-fidelity system modeling. A novel distributed frequency response (DFR) model is developed that incorporates hydraulic states (e.g., pressure heads in complicated pipelines and surge tank water levels) and network topology, offering improved accuracy over conventional average system frequency (ASF) models. Based on this model, a multi-input multi-output model predictive control (MIMO-MPC) scheme is designed to track the power allocation setpoint and enable wind turbines to participate in LFC in coordination with synchronous generators. Simulation results on 6-bus and IEEE 39-bus systems demonstrate the proposed strategy’s superiority in frequency regulation. Under variable wind conditions, it reduces the integral of time-weighted absolute error (ITAE) of frequency deviation for the PSU by 47.3% compared to the PI control. These outcomes validate the enhanced transient performance and robustness of the scheme for practical smart grid applications.

title: Modeling and Impact Assessment of Load-Altering Attacks in TSO-DSO Coordinated Power Systems
abstract: At the intersection of multi-layer grid operations and emerging cyber-physical threats, lies the critical challenge of ensuring secure and resilient coordination between transmission system operators (TSOs) and distribution system operators (DSOs). While most existing studies focus on the operational optimization of TSO-DSO interactions, the increasing deployment of IoT-controllable loads raises concerns about cyber vulnerabilities. This paper presents a unified modeling framework for evaluating the impacts of load-altering attacks (LAAs) within an AC-AC coordinated TSO-DSO environment. An LAA strategy is developed that originates at the distribution level and propagates upward through TSO-DSO coordination. This “bottom-up” propagation reveals systemic interdependencies and vulnerabilities across grid layers. To capture a range of attacker capabilities, we model representative adversaries (black-box, white-box, and grey-box) each reflecting different levels of system observability and access, and aiming to disrupt grid operations and exploit market dynamics to increase profits from their controlled distributed resources, considering heterogeneity of local resources and contractual arrangements to improve the realism of the market-based coordination framework. Case studies demonstrate how LAAs disrupt locational marginal prices, power flows, and distributed energy resource operations. The results reveal systemic vulnerabilities to coordinated cyber-physical threats and expose hidden weaknesses of grid coordination mechanisms.

title: Scalable Building HVAC Control Through Laxity-Based Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Demand flexibility is playing a vital role in maintaining grid power balance, reducing peak demand, and saving energy bills. Given their highly shiftable characteristics and significant contribution to a building’s energy consumption, Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems can provide valuable demand flexibility to the power systems by adjusting their power consumption in response to electricity price and power system needs. To exploit such flexibility in terms of both operation time and demand level, modeling and efficient aggregation techniques of HVAC load flexibility are investigated in this paper. To tackle the curse of dimensionality issue associated with an increasing number of HVAC devices, the notion of laxity for HVAC is proposed in this work to quantify the urgency level of each building’s operation request. Considering the inherent complexity and uncertainty presented in HVAC systems, we design a novel deep reinforcement learning (RL)-based controller to schedule the aggregate dispatched power based on the efficient representation of aggregated laxity information as well as the electricity price. For each HVAC load, only laxity information is revealed instead of full states, and integrated with proposed RL agent using least-laxity-first (LLF) rule for power allocation. To validate the superior efficiency and performance provided by our laxity-based RL agent, we evaluate the temperature control and the energy cost savings of a large number of HVACs in both single-zone and multi-zone scenarios under varying climate and electricity market conditions. Our data-driven approach also significantly saves the modeling and data burden compared to model-based controllers. Empirically, numerical results also indicate that the proposed approach outperforms standard RL with full HVAC states. Compared to the widely used deep RL baseline, it achieves up to 42% reduction in total energy cost while maintaining comparable average temperature deviation.

title: Adaptive Fast Clearing Algorithm-Based Peer-to-Peer Transaction for Microgrid-Integrated Distribution Network Considering Uncertainty
abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) transaction has become an effective way to improve the economic efficiency of microgrids (MGs). However, existing studies neglect the impacts of electricity power-carbon-green certificate join cost (PCGC), energy-reserve co-optimization and uncertainty within MG on P2P transactions schemes. To fill this gap, this paper proposes a P2P transaction framework for interconnected MG, where carbon allowance-green certificate constraints, reserve constraints, joint chance constraints are employed respectively to capture PCGC coupling, reserve provisioning, and uncertainty impacts. An optimization-based piecewise-linear marginal utility function (MUF) is developed to characterize MG’s price-responsive behaviors under multi-resource coordination. Furthermore, an adaptive fast clearing algorithm (AFCA) is designed with a network-fee-exempt non-iterative clearing scheme and a network-fee-incorporated oscillation-resistant iterative scheme to ensure computational efficiency and distribution network security. Numerical results demonstrate that the MUF effectively captures the impacts of internal reserve, network constraints, risk preference, and PCGC on inter-MG P2P trading behaviors. The AFCA significantly accelerates computation, with a 97.72% time reduction compared to the widely used alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) in a 5-MG system, and solves the 20-MG system in only 1.45 s with an optimality error of merely 0.59%.

title: Sharding-Based Asynchronous Coordination for Secure and Scalable Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading Under Delays and Attacks
abstract: The proliferation of distributed energy resources has enabled the emergence of prosumers and peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading. However, many existing decentralized market clearing schemes that require iterative message exchanges are vulnerable to false data injection (FDI) and can stall under heterogeneous communication delays. Blockchain solutions enhance integrity but often rely on synchronous optimization and global consensus, yielding excessive overhead. In this paper, a sharding-based asynchronous coordination mechanism for network-constrained P2P energy trading is developed. First, an asynchronous decentralized optimization method is developed to clear the market with respect to network constraints. Second, a dynamic sharding method is proposed to partition prosumers into low-latency shards by jointly considering trading relationships and communication delays, thereby localizing coordination and reducing cross-network synchronization. Third, a lightweight consensus mechanism that integrates asynchronous updates with a chained verification structure is designed to verify message correctness and detect malicious behaviors, thereby enabling fast intrashard agreement without the need for global synchronous rounds. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed approach preserves scalability and reduces the overall runtime by 79.15% compared with benchmark mechanisms while maintaining secure clearing performance under attack scenarios.

title: Future Trajectory Representation-Aided DRL for Real-Time Battery Energy Storage Dispatch in Distribution Networks
abstract: Dispatching battery energy storage systems (BESS) in distributed grids is challenging due to the sequential nature of the decision-making process, which needs to account for future uncertainties in system states and time-coupling constraints. Numerous forecasting techniques have been developed to capture such uncertainties, but most prioritize accuracy alone, and their potential for enhancing optimization performance has rarely been studied.
